explanation.C: Incorrect. "Subsequently" means "afterward," but the Portuguese reached Madeira around 1420, while Zheng He's voyages were still under way. This is the closest near miss.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The Portuguese voyages were not a result of Zheng He's voyages; the text links them only in time.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: Acousticians describe a room's reverberation time as the number of seconds a sound takes to fade by sixty decibels after its source stops. A long reverberation time, around two seconds or more, lets the notes of choral or organ music blend into a rich, continuous sound, which is one reason many large stone churches are prized as venues for such music. ______ a short reverberation time, closer to one second, suits speech and drama, since each syllable fades before the next one can blur it.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Conversely,
choices.B: Nevertheless,
choices.C: For example,
choices.D: Similarly,

explanation.why: The second sentence says a long reverberation time suits blended music. The last sentence states the reverse case: a short reverberation time suits speech. The transition must introduce the opposite side of the same relationship.
explanation.A: Correct. "Conversely" signals that the last sentence reverses the previous case: short instead of long, speech instead of choral music.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Nevertheless" signals that something is true in spite of what came before, but short reverberation suiting speech does not go against long reverberation suiting choral music. This is the closest near miss.
explanation.C: Incorrect. A short reverberation time for speech is not an example of a long reverberation time suiting music.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Similarly" signals a parallel point, but the last sentence describes the opposite case, not a matching one.

items.subject: science
items.passage: The platypus departs from the usual pattern of mammalian life in several ways. Females lay leathery eggs rather than giving birth to live young, and after the eggs hatch, they feed their young on milk that seeps from patches of skin on the belly, since they have no nipples. ______ adult males are among the very few venomous mammals: each carries a sharp spur on the ankle of each hind leg that can deliver venom strong enough to disable a small animal and to cause intense, lasting pain in humans.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Specifically,
choices.B: Moreover,
choices.C: Nevertheless,
choices.D: Consequently,

explanation.why: The first sentence says the platypus is unusual "in several ways." The second sentence gives the first set of ways (egg laying and milk without nipples). The last sentence adds a further, separate way: males are venomous. The transition must add another point in support of the same claim.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Specifically" would introduce a more detailed account of the previous sentence, but venom has nothing to do with eggs or milk. It is a separate example of how the platypus is unusual. This is the closest near miss.
explanation.B: Correct. "Moreover" adds venom as one more way in which the platypus differs from most mammals.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Nevertheless" signals a contrast, but being venomous is another unusual trait, which supports the first sentence.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Males are not venomous because females lay eggs; the two traits are independent.

items.subject: science
items.passage: Most biologists do not classify viruses as living organisms, chiefly because a virus cannot reproduce or carry out metabolism on its own: outside a host cell, it is an inert package of genetic material wrapped in protein. The discovery in 2003 of mimivirus, a virus larger than some bacteria, prompted renewed debate, but it has not overturned this view. ______ mimivirus and the other giant viruses identified since then carry genes for some of the molecular machinery that cells use to build proteins, machinery that ordinary viruses lack. Yet none of these viruses possesses ribosomes, the structures in which proteins are actually assembled, so even the largest of them remain wholly dependent on the cells they infect.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: For example,
choices.B: Consequently,
choices.C: Indeed,
choices.D: Granted,

explanation.why: The author's position is that giant viruses have not overturned the view that viruses are not alive. The sentence with the blank states a fact that seems to favor the other side (the genes for protein-building machinery), and the next sentence begins "Yet," returning to the author's position. The blank must introduce a concession.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The genes are not an example of the view remaining intact; they are evidence that seems to challenge it.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The genes are not a result of the view surviving; they are what made the debate arise.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Indeed" would strengthen the preceding claim that the view has not been overturned, but the genes for protein-building machinery point the other way. This is the most tempting choice because it would fit if the passage stopped after "prompted renewed debate."
explanation.D: Correct. "Granted" concedes a point in favor of the opposing view before "Yet" explains why that point is not decisive.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: In the early nineteenth century, the mills of Dundee, Scotland, spun mainly flax, much of it imported from Russia, although a few had begun experimenting with jute, a coarse fiber grown chiefly in Bengal that was cheaper than flax but harder to spin. When the Crimean War broke out in 1853, eventually setting Britain and Russia on opposing sides, the supply of Russian flax to British mills was disrupted. ______ Dundee's manufacturers turned to jute on a far larger scale, and within a few decades the city had become so closely identified with the fiber that it was nicknamed "Juteopolis."
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Nevertheless,
choices.B: Consequently,
choices.C: In other words,
choices.D: For instance,

explanation.why: The second sentence describes a cause: the war cut off Russian flax. The last sentence describes what the mills did in response: they shifted to jute on a large scale. The transition must signal a result.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Nevertheless" would mean the mills turned to jute in spite of the flax shortage, but the shortage is the reason they turned to jute. This choice can tempt a reader who recalls that jute was "harder to spin," but that detail is not what the blank responds to.
explanation.B: Correct. "Consequently" shows that the large-scale turn to jute followed from the loss of Russian flax.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The last sentence reports a new development, not a restatement of the flax shortage.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The shift to jute is a response to the flax shortage, not an example of it.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: Designers of traditional Japanese gardens have long used a technique called shakkei, often translated as "borrowed scenery." In a garden built on this principle, a distant mountain, a temple roof, or a stand of trees beyond the property is not merely visible from within; it is deliberately framed by hedges, walls, and carefully placed plantings that conceal whatever lies in between, so that the remote view seems to continue the foreground without interruption. ______ the landscape beyond the garden's boundary is treated as one of the garden's own elements, even though the designer neither owns nor controls it.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: For instance,
choices.B: In other words,
choices.C: Similarly,
choices.D: By contrast,

explanation.why: The second sentence explains in detail how a shakkei garden frames a distant view so that it seems part of the garden. The last sentence sums up that same idea in plainer terms: the outside landscape becomes one of the garden's elements, which is what "borrowed scenery" means. A restatement transition is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The last sentence is a general summary of the technique, not a particular example of it; the examples (a mountain, a temple roof, trees) came earlier.
explanation.B: Correct. "In other words" signals that the last sentence restates what borrowing scenery amounts to.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Similarly" introduces a separate case that resembles the first, but the last sentence describes the same technique, not a parallel one.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "By contrast" signals a difference, but the last sentence agrees with and summarizes the previous one. It may tempt readers who notice the phrase "neither owns nor controls," but that phrase is part of the same idea, not a contrast with the sentence before.

items.subject: literature
items.passage: Eleanor had rehearsed, through the whole of the long drive from the station, the speech in which she would tell her aunt that she had accepted the teaching position in Chicago; she had polished its apologies and anticipated its objections until it seemed to her very nearly unanswerable. But when the carriage drew up and she saw the old woman waiting on the step, a shawl pulled tight against the wind and one thin hand raised in greeting, the speech deserted her entirely. ______ she heard herself asking after the roses, and the new cook, and the health of the minister's wife, as though she had come home to stay.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Instead,
choices.B: Moreover,
choices.C: Likewise,
choices.D: Nevertheless,

explanation.why: The second sentence says Eleanor's prepared speech "deserted her," so she does not give it. The last sentence describes what she says in its place: small talk about roses, the cook, and a neighbor. The transition must introduce what happened in place of the speech.
explanation.A: Correct. "Instead" signals that the small talk took the place of the speech Eleanor had planned.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Moreover" adds a further point of the same kind, but the small talk is not an addition to the speech; the speech never happens.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Likewise" signals a similar point, but asking about roses is not similar to forgetting a speech.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Nevertheless" would mean Eleanor made small talk in spite of losing her speech, but losing the speech does not work against small talk; the small talk fills the gap the speech left. This is the most tempting choice because the passage is full of contrast.

items.subject: science
items.passage: Collisions with the rotating blades of wind turbines kill a considerable number of birds each year, particularly large raptors such as eagles. At a wind farm on the Norwegian island of Smøla, researchers tested a simple remedy: on four turbines, they painted one of the three blades black, a change thought to reduce the motion blur that may make spinning blades hard for birds to see. Over the following years, recorded bird deaths at the painted turbines fell by roughly 70 percent compared with nearby unpainted ones. ______ the study involved only a handful of turbines at a single site, and its authors have called for larger trials before the method is widely adopted.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Specifically,
choices.B: Moreover,
choices.C: Instead,
choices.D: However,

explanation.why: The third sentence reports an encouraging result. The last sentence points out a limitation of that result: the study was small and limited to one site. The transition must introduce a qualification that contrasts with the encouraging finding without denying it.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Specifically" would introduce a precise detail about the 70 percent drop, but the last sentence shifts to the study's limits.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Moreover" would add another point in favor of the method, but the small size of the study is a reason for caution, not further support. This is the most tempting choice because the sentence does add information.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Instead" would mean the small size of the study replaces the result, but the result still stands; it is only limited.
explanation.D: Correct. "However" signals that the promising result comes with an important limitation.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: Historians once traced the spread of papermaking from China to the Islamic world to a single dramatic episode. According to this account, Chinese prisoners captured at the Battle of Talas in 751 taught the craft to their captors in Samarkand, from which it soon reached Baghdad and, centuries later, Europe. Many scholars now regard the story with skepticism, observing that it appears only in sources written long after the battle and that paper seems to have been known in Central Asia well before 751. ______ they propose that the technique traveled westward gradually, carried along trade routes by merchants and artisans over generations rather than introduced in a single stroke.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Instead,
choices.B: For example,
choices.C: Nevertheless,
choices.D: Likewise,

explanation.why: The third sentence says scholars doubt the single-episode story. The last sentence gives the account these scholars put in its place: a gradual spread along trade routes. The transition must introduce an alternative to an idea just rejected.
explanation.A: Correct. "Instead" signals that the gradual-spread account replaces the doubted single-episode story.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The gradual-spread account is not an example of the scholars' skepticism; it is their alternative explanation.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Nevertheless" would mean scholars propose a gradual spread in spite of their skepticism, but their skepticism is exactly what leads them to the new account. This is the closest near miss.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Likewise" signals a similar point, but the new account differs from the old story rather than resembling it.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: Painters have traditionally mixed their colors on a palette before applying them, but Georges Seurat, working in Paris in the 1880s, sought to let the viewer's eye do much of that mixing instead. ______ he applied small, separate dots of comparatively unmixed color side by side, so that, seen from a suitable distance, neighboring dots would merge in perception rather than on the canvas. Seurat believed, drawing on the color science of his day, that such optical mixing would produce more luminous effects than pigments blended beforehand, though critics have since debated whether his technique achieves that aim.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Similarly,
choices.B: For example,
choices.C: Nevertheless,
choices.D: Specifically,

explanation.why: The first sentence states Seurat's general aim: to let the viewer's eye do the mixing. The second sentence explains exactly how he pursued that aim, with separate dots that merge at a distance. The transition must introduce a precise description of the method just mentioned in general terms.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Similarly" introduces a separate but parallel idea, yet the second sentence explains the same idea in detail.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "For example" would present the dots as one instance among several ways Seurat let the eye mix color, but the sentence describes his method itself, not one case of it. This is the most attractive near miss.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Nevertheless" signals a contrast, but the dot technique carries out Seurat's aim rather than working against it.
explanation.D: Correct. "Specifically" signals that the second sentence spells out exactly how Seurat let the viewer's eye mix colors.

items.subject: science
items.passage: Convergent evolution, the independent appearance of similar traits in lineages that are not closely related, has usually been documented in anatomy: the wings of bats and birds, for instance, or the streamlined bodies of sharks and dolphins. Researchers comparing genetic sequences have now identified a number of cases in which convergence extends to the level of individual molecules. ______ echolocating bats and toothed whales, two groups whose common ancestor could not echolocate, share several of the same amino acid changes in prestin, a protein in the inner ear involved in hearing high-frequency sounds.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Nevertheless,
choices.B: For example,
choices.C: Accordingly,
choices.D: Specifically,

explanation.why: The second sentence says researchers have found "a number of cases" of molecular convergence. The last sentence describes one such case: matching changes in prestin in bats and toothed whales. The transition must introduce one instance of a general claim about several cases.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Nevertheless" signals a contrast, but the prestin case supports the claim about molecular convergence.
explanation.B: Correct. "For example" signals that the prestin case is one of the "number of cases" just mentioned.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The shared prestin changes are not a result of researchers comparing sequences; the comparison revealed them.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Specifically" would present the bat and whale case as a more precise statement of the whole claim, but the claim covers "a number of cases," and this is only one of them. This is the most attractive near miss.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: A widely repeated story holds that medieval Europeans believed the Earth to be flat until explorers such as Columbus proved otherwise. Historians of science have found little support for it. Granted, a few early Christian writers, most notably Lactantius in the early fourth century, did reject the idea of a spherical Earth, and popular images of the world were not always consistent. ______ the Earth's roundness was taken for granted by most educated people throughout the Middle Ages: it was assumed in the writings of the English scholar Bede in the eighth century and taught in universities from the thirteenth century onward through astronomy textbooks such as Sacrobosco's On the Sphere.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: In other words,
choices.B: Still,
choices.C: Moreover,
choices.D: Consequently,

explanation.why: The third sentence begins "Granted," conceding some evidence that seems to favor the flat-Earth story. The last sentence returns to the author's main point: educated medieval people assumed a round Earth. The transition must signal a return to the main claim despite the concession.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "In other words" would restate the concession, but the last sentence says nearly the opposite. It may tempt readers who connect it to the second sentence, but the concession comes in between.
explanation.B: Correct. "Still" signals that, despite the conceded exceptions, a round Earth was the standard educated view.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Moreover" would add a point in the same direction as the sentence before, but the last sentence pushes against the concession about Lactantius instead of extending it.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Medieval belief in a round Earth is not a result of a few writers rejecting the idea; it holds despite them.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: In nineteenth-century Delhi, Persian remained the prestigious language of literary prose, and letters written in it customarily opened with long strings of ornate salutations and elaborate praise of the recipient. The poet Mirza Ghalib, who regarded his Persian verse as his most serious work, nonetheless wrote many of his later letters to friends in Urdu, the everyday language of the city. ______ he largely abandoned the customary openings, often greeting a friend simply by name and moving straight to news, complaints, and jokes, so that his letters read less like formal compositions than like conversations on paper.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Specifically,
choices.B: Moreover,
choices.C: Nevertheless,
choices.D: For instance,

explanation.why: The text describes two ways Ghalib's letters broke with custom. The second sentence gives the first: he wrote in Urdu rather than Persian. The last sentence adds a second, separate break: he dropped the ornate openings. The transition must add a further point of the same kind.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Specifically" would present the dropped openings as a detailed account of writing in Urdu, but choosing a language and choosing a style of greeting are separate decisions. This is the most attractive near miss.
explanation.B: Correct. "Moreover" adds Ghalib's abandonment of ornate openings as a second departure from custom.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Nevertheless" signals a contrast, but dropping the ornate openings goes in the same direction as writing in everyday Urdu.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Abandoning the openings is not an example of writing in Urdu; one could write in Urdu and still use ornate openings.

items.subject: science
items.passage: Air bubbles sealed in polar ice preserve samples of the ancient atmosphere, and cores drilled at Dome C in Antarctica hold a record reaching back roughly 800,000 years. The way bubbles form complicates that record. Fresh snow is slowly compressed into firn and then into ice, and its pores stay open to the air above until they close off at depth, a process that can take centuries or even millennia. The gas in a bubble is therefore younger than the ice around it. ______ before researchers can compare past carbon dioxide levels with temperatures inferred from the ice itself, they must estimate this age difference, which at a cold, dry site such as Dome C can reach several thousand years.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: However,
choices.B: Accordingly,
choices.C: Similarly,
choices.D: Specifically,

explanation.why: The fourth sentence establishes that the gas in a bubble is younger than the surrounding ice. The last sentence states what researchers must do because of that fact: estimate the age difference before comparing records. The transition must signal that the last sentence follows from the one before it.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "However" signals a contrast, but needing to estimate the age gap follows from the gap rather than contrasting with it. It may tempt a reader who notices that the passage describes a complication.
explanation.B: Correct. "Accordingly" signals that researchers must estimate the age difference because the gas is younger than the ice.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Similarly" introduces a parallel case, but the last sentence describes a consequence of the same fact, not a similar fact.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Specifically" would introduce a precise detail about how the gas is younger, but the last sentence moves on to what researchers must do about it.

items.subject: literature
items.passage: For thirty years Nasreen's grandmother in Hyderabad had cooked the family's Eid nihari without a written recipe, measuring the spices by the cupped palm of her hand and judging the broth by its smell. Nasreen had watched her do it every year and had, at last, copied down every step in a notebook, with the quantities converted into teaspoons and minutes. ______ when she stood alone at the stove on her first Eid in Lahore, the notebook propped against the spice tin, the dish came out tasting faintly wrong, and she could not have said which of the hundred small judgments she had failed to make.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Similarly,
choices.B: Even so,
choices.C: Accordingly,
choices.D: Instead,

explanation.why: The second sentence suggests Nasreen should succeed: she watched for years and wrote down every step. The last sentence reports that the dish still came out wrong. The transition must signal an outcome that goes against what the earlier preparation would lead a reader to expect.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Similarly" signals a parallel point, but the failed dish contrasts with Nasreen's careful preparation.
explanation.B: Correct. "Even so" signals that the dish went wrong despite Nasreen's careful notes.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Accordingly" means "as a result," but careful notes would lead us to expect success, not a dish that tastes wrong.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Instead" would mean the failed dish replaced something mentioned before, but Nasreen's notes and her cooking are not alternatives; she uses the notebook while she cooks. This is the closest near miss.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: When employees must actively sign up for a workplace retirement savings plan, participation is often modest; in studies of US firms, a third or more of eligible workers have commonly failed to enroll. When the same kind of plan instead enrolls workers automatically, leaving them free to opt out at any time, participation frequently rises above 85 percent. Nothing else need differ between the two arrangements: the contribution options, the employer's matching funds, and the freedom to join or leave can be identical. ______ the large gap in participation must be attributed to the default itself, that is, to which outcome occurs for employees who never make an active choice.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Likewise,
choices.B: However,
choices.C: Thus,
choices.D: For example,

explanation.why: The text establishes two premises: participation differs sharply between the two arrangements, and nothing but the default differs between them. The last sentence draws the conclusion these premises support: the default must explain the gap. A transition that signals a conclusion is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Likewise" introduces a similar point, but the last sentence is a conclusion drawn from the previous points, not another point of the same kind.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "However" would signal that the last sentence contrasts with the one before it, but the conclusion depends on the identical incentives rather than conflicting with them. It is tempting because the passage contrasts two participation rates, but that contrast comes earlier.
explanation.C: Correct. "Thus" signals that the last sentence is the conclusion that follows from the two premises.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The last sentence is a conclusion about all such plans, not an example of identical incentives.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: John Cage's 4′33″ (1952) instructs its performers to make no intentional sound for the work's duration of four minutes and thirty-three seconds, and audiences have sometimes received it as a provocation or a joke. Cage had come to believe that true silence does not exist, a conviction strengthened by a visit to a soundproof chamber in which he still heard sounds that he attributed to his own body. He therefore rejected the idea that the piece consists of silence. ______ he intended the work to turn listeners' attention to the sounds that are always present, such as rustling programs, distant traffic, and the breathing of the audience, and to invite them to hear those sounds as music.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: For instance,
choices.B: Rather,
choices.C: Nevertheless,
choices.D: Similarly,

explanation.why: The third sentence says Cage rejected one description of the piece: that it consists of silence. The last sentence gives the description he accepted in its place: the piece directs attention to ever-present sounds. The transition must introduce a correction that replaces a rejected idea.
explanation.A: Incorrect. What Cage intended is not an example of his rejecting the idea of silence; it is the view he held instead.
explanation.B: Correct. "Rather" signals that the last sentence states what the piece is in place of what Cage said it is not.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Nevertheless" would mean Cage intended the work to highlight ambient sound in spite of rejecting the idea of silence, but that rejection is exactly why he saw the piece this way. This is the closest near miss.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Similarly" introduces a parallel idea, but the last sentence states Cage's alternative view rather than a view like the one he rejected.

items.subject: science
items.passage: In an experiment begun in 1963 on a rocky shore in Washington State, the ecologist Robert Paine repeatedly removed the predatory sea star Pisaster ochraceus from one stretch of shoreline while leaving a neighboring stretch untouched. Without the sea stars to eat them, mussels spread across the rock and crowded out many other species, and the number of species in the experimental area fell sharply. ______ after wolves were eliminated from Yellowstone National Park in the early twentieth century, elk populations grew and, according to many ecologists, browsed streamside willows and aspens so heavily that the habitats those trees supported declined.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Nevertheless,
choices.B: In other words,
choices.C: For instance,
choices.D: Similarly,

explanation.why: The first two sentences describe one case: removing a predator let its prey spread and harmed many other species. The last sentence describes a different place and predator with the same pattern. The transition must link two separate cases that resemble each other.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Nevertheless" signals a contrast, but the Yellowstone case matches the sea star case instead of contrasting with it.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "In other words" would mean the Yellowstone sentence restates the sea star finding, but it describes a different ecosystem, predator, and time. This is the most attractive near miss.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "For instance" would make Yellowstone an example of Paine's experiment, but the passage makes no general claim for it to illustrate; it describes one specific experiment, and Yellowstone is a separate, parallel case.
explanation.D: Correct. "Similarly" signals that losing wolves in Yellowstone had an effect like that of removing sea stars from the shore.

items.subject: science
items.passage: The sand cat lives in the deserts of North Africa, Arabia, and Central Asia, where the ground can become painfully hot by midday. Unlike most cats, it has a thick mat of fur growing across the pads of its paws. ______ the sand cat can walk on scorching sand without burning its feet, and the soft fur leaves almost no tracks for predators or prey to follow.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: However,
choices.B: For example,
choices.C: Similarly,
choices.D: As a result,

explanation.why: The second sentence describes a feature: fur on the paw pads. The last sentence describes what that feature allows the cat to do: walk on hot sand and leave few tracks. A cause-and-effect transition is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "However" signals a contrast, but walking safely on hot sand follows from the furry paws rather than contrasting with them.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Walking on hot sand is not an example of having furry paws; it is what the fur makes possible.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Similarly" would introduce a parallel feature, but the last sentence describes a consequence of the fur, not another feature like it.
explanation.D: Correct. "As a result" shows that walking on hot sand without harm is the effect of the furry paws.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: In most big cities, construction crews surround a rising building with scaffolding made of steel tubes. In Hong Kong, scaffolding is still often built from bamboo poles tied together with strips of plastic. Bamboo is light enough for a worker to carry several poles at once, and it costs far less than steel. ______ it is strong enough that workers use it on buildings dozens of stories tall.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: For example,
choices.B: Instead,
choices.C: Moreover,
choices.D: Consequently,

explanation.why: The third sentence lists two advantages of bamboo: it is light and cheap. The last sentence adds a third advantage, its strength. A transition that adds another point of the same kind is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Bamboo's strength is not an example of its being light or cheap; it is a separate advantage.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Instead" would mean that strength replaces the advantages just listed, but the sentence adds to them.
explanation.C: Correct. "Moreover" adds the strength of bamboo to the other advantages already named.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Bamboo is not strong because it is light and cheap; the last sentence adds a new point rather than stating a result.

items.subject: literature
items.passage: By the time Tomas finished clearing the snow from his own front steps, his gloves were soaked and his fingers had gone numb. The warm kitchen was only a few feet away, and he could smell the bread his mother had just taken out of the oven. ______ he picked up the shovel again and crossed the street to Mrs. Varga's house, because he knew that at eighty-three she could not clear her own path.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Even so,
choices.B: In other words,
choices.C: Therefore,
choices.D: For instance,

explanation.why: The first two sentences explain why Tomas would want to go inside: he is cold and wet, and warm bread is waiting. The last sentence says he kept working anyway. A transition that signals an action taken despite the reasons just given is needed.
explanation.A: Correct. "Even so" shows that Tomas went on shoveling in spite of his numb fingers and the warm kitchen.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "In other words" would restate the previous idea, but the last sentence describes a new action, not the same idea in different words.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Therefore" would mean the cold and the bread caused him to keep shoveling, but they are reasons to stop.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Crossing the street to shovel is not an example of being cold or smelling bread.

items.subject: science
items.passage: In most coastal places, the sea level rises and falls by one or two meters between low tide and high tide. A few bays with the right shape and size, however, funnel the incoming water so that the tide climbs much higher. ______ in the Bay of Fundy, on the Atlantic coast of Canada, the difference between low and high tide can reach 16 meters, roughly the height of a five-story building.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Nevertheless,
choices.B: For example,
choices.C: In addition,
choices.D: As a result,

explanation.why: The second sentence makes a general claim: some bays funnel the tide so that it climbs much higher than usual. The last sentence describes one specific bay where the tide reaches 16 meters. A transition that introduces an example is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Nevertheless" signals that something is true despite the previous point, but the Bay of Fundy supports the previous point.
explanation.B: Correct. "For example" introduces the Bay of Fundy as a specific case of a bay with unusually high tides.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "In addition" would add a separate new point, but the last sentence illustrates the claim already made rather than adding to it.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The 16-meter tide is not caused by the general claim about bays; it is one case of that claim.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: The Newar people of the Kathmandu Valley in Nepal have a long tradition of carving wood. The old houses and temples around Patan Durbar Square are decorated with wooden windows whose frames are cut into dense patterns of flowers, birds, and figures. ______ one window near the square is carved as a circle of overlapping lattice so fine that it looks more like lace than like wood.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: As a result,
choices.B: On the other hand,
choices.C: For instance,
choices.D: Likewise,

explanation.why: The second sentence makes a general statement: Newar windows are carved with dense patterns. The last sentence describes one particular window that shows this skill. A transition that introduces an example is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The lace-like window is not an effect of the other windows being carved; it is one of them.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "On the other hand" signals a contrast, but the lace-like window agrees with the description of finely carved windows.
explanation.C: Correct. "For instance" introduces the lace-like window as a specific example of the carved windows just described.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Likewise" would introduce a separate, similar case, but the window is part of the same tradition already described, not a parallel to it.

items.subject: science
items.passage: The dromedary camel is well suited to dry, sandy places. It can close its nostrils tightly, which keeps blowing sand out of its nose during a desert windstorm. ______ the inside of its nose is lined with folds that cool the air the camel breathes out, so that moisture condenses on them and is recovered instead of being lost to the dry desert air.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: For example,
choices.B: In contrast,
choices.C: In addition,
choices.D: Therefore,

explanation.why: The second sentence describes one feature of the camel's nose: nostrils that close against sand. The last sentence describes a second, separate feature: folds that recover moisture. A transition that adds another point is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Recovering moisture is not an example of closing the nostrils against sand; it is a different adaptation.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "In contrast" signals a difference, but both sentences describe features that help the camel in the desert.
explanation.C: Correct. "In addition" adds the moisture-recovering folds to the first feature of the nose already described.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The folds that recover moisture are not a result of the nostrils closing; they are a separate feature.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: At an exhibition in New York in 1854, the inventor Elisha Otis stood on a raised platform held up by a single rope and ordered the rope cut. The crowd expected the platform to crash, but a safety brake caught it after it dropped only a few inches. ______ Otis sold his safety elevators to one building owner after another, and in 1857 the first passenger elevator with his brake opened in a New York store.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: For example,
choices.B: Afterward,
choices.C: Likewise,
choices.D: Nevertheless,

explanation.why: The text tells a story in time order. First Otis performs his demonstration in 1854; then he sells elevators, and the first passenger elevator opens in 1857. A transition that shows the next stage in a sequence is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Selling elevators is not an example of the demonstration; it is what happened after it.
explanation.B: Correct. "Afterward" shows that the sales and the 1857 passenger elevator came after the 1854 demonstration.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Likewise" signals a similar point, but selling elevators is a later event, not a parallel to the demonstration.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Nevertheless" signals that something happened despite the previous point, but the demonstration's success helped Otis sell elevators.

items.subject: literature
items.passage: Hina had watched her aunt slap rounds of dough onto the hot clay wall of the tandoor hundreds of times, and the motion looked as easy as closing a door. ______ when her aunt finally let her try, the dough stuck to her fingers, folded on itself, and slid down the wall into the coals, where it burned to a crisp before she could reach it.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: However,
choices.B: Similarly,
choices.C: Therefore,
choices.D: In other words,

explanation.why: The first sentence says the motion "looked as easy as closing a door." The second sentence describes Hina's attempt, which went badly. A transition that signals a contrast between how easy it looked and how hard it was is needed.
explanation.A: Correct. "However" signals the contrast between how easy the task appeared and what happened when Hina tried it.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Similarly" signals a matching idea, but Hina's failed attempt is the opposite of the easy motion she had watched.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Therefore" would mean the dough fell because the motion looked easy, but the sentence shows that the appearance was misleading.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "In other words" would restate the first sentence, but the second sentence describes a different event.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: For more than a thousand years, most writing in Europe was done with iron gall ink. To make it, ink makers first gathered oak galls, the small round growths that form on oak twigs around the eggs of certain wasps. They crushed the galls and soaked them in water to draw out their acids. ______ they stirred in iron salts and a little gum, and the mixture turned a deep blue-black as it met the air.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Next,
choices.B: In contrast,
choices.C: Nevertheless,
choices.D: For example,

explanation.why: The text describes the steps of making ink in order: ink makers "first gathered oak galls," then crushed and soaked them. The last sentence gives the step that came after soaking. A transition that marks the next step in a sequence is needed.
explanation.A: Correct. "Next" shows that stirring in iron salts was the step that followed soaking the crushed galls.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "In contrast" signals a difference, but adding iron salts is simply the following step, not an opposing idea.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Nevertheless" signals something done despite the previous step, but there is no obstacle in the text for the ink makers to overcome.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Adding iron salts is not an example of soaking the galls; it is a separate step.

items.subject: science
items.passage: A zeer is a simple cooler made from two clay pots, one placed inside the other, with the gap between them filled with wet sand. As water in the sand slowly evaporates through the outer pot, it carries heat away from the inner pot. ______ the zeer works on the same principle that cools a person's skin when sweat dries. In a dry climate, vegetables kept inside can stay fresh for days longer than they would in open air.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: For instance,
choices.B: In other words,
choices.C: Nevertheless,
choices.D: Afterward,

explanation.why: The second sentence explains how the cooler works: evaporating water carries heat away. The third sentence explains the same idea again in a more familiar way, by comparing it to sweat drying on skin. A transition that introduces a restatement is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Sweat cooling the skin is not an example of the zeer; it is a comparison used to restate how the zeer works.
explanation.B: Correct. "In other words" introduces the sweat comparison as a simpler way of saying how the evaporating water cools the pot.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Nevertheless" signals a contrast, but the comparison to sweat agrees with the explanation just given.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Afterward" signals the next event in time, but the sentence does not describe a later step.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: True cinnamon comes from the inner bark of a small tree grown mainly in the southwest of Sri Lanka, near the town of Galle. Harvesting it is delicate work. The outer bark must be scraped away and the thin inner bark peeled off in long strips without tearing it. ______ most of the harvest is still done by hand, by skilled peelers who learn the craft from their parents and grandparents.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Similarly,
choices.B: In contrast,
choices.C: For example,
choices.D: Consequently,

explanation.why: The third sentence explains that the inner bark must be removed carefully "without tearing it." The last sentence states what follows from this: the work is still done by hand by skilled peelers. A cause-and-effect transition is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Similarly" signals a parallel point, but the last sentence is a consequence of the delicate work, not a point like it.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "In contrast" signals a difference, but hand peeling follows from the careful work the text describes rather than contrasting with it.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Peeling by hand is not an example of scraping away the outer bark; it is the result of the work being so delicate.
explanation.D: Correct. "Consequently" shows that the harvest is done by hand because the peeling is so delicate.

items.subject: literature
items.passage: My grandmother kept an album of pressed flowers that she had started as a girl. Each one lay flat between sheets of tissue paper, and over sixty years the bright petals had faded to shades of brown and gray, so that a rose and a poppy now looked almost the same. ______ when I turned the pages with her, she could name every flower and tell me the field, the garden, or the roadside where she had picked it.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Nevertheless,
choices.B: For example,
choices.C: As a result,
choices.D: Likewise,

explanation.why: The second sentence says the flowers have faded so much that different kinds "looked almost the same." The last sentence says the grandmother could still identify every one. A transition that signals something true in spite of the previous point is needed.
explanation.A: Correct. "Nevertheless" shows that the grandmother could name every flower even though the faded petals all looked alike.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Naming each flower is not an example of the flowers fading; it goes against what the fading would lead you to expect.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "As a result" would mean the fading caused her to know each flower, but her knowledge exists despite the fading.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Likewise" signals a similar idea, but being able to name the flowers is unlike their having become hard to tell apart.

items.subject: science
items.passage: A tumbleweed starts its life as an ordinary rooted plant. In late summer, after it has flowered, the whole plant dries out and its stem becomes brittle at the base. A strong wind then snaps the dead plant free, and it begins to roll across the open ground. ______ it scatters its seeds, dropping a few at a time over a distance that can stretch for kilometers.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: For instance,
choices.B: Along the way,
choices.C: In contrast,
choices.D: Even so,

explanation.why: The text describes what happens to a tumbleweed in order: it dries, snaps free, and rolls across the ground. The last sentence describes what happens while it rolls: it drops seeds. A transition that connects this action to the rolling journey is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Dropping seeds is not an example of the plant rolling; it is what the plant does as it rolls.
explanation.B: Correct. "Along the way" shows that the seeds are scattered during the plant's rolling journey across the ground.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "In contrast" signals a difference, but scattering seeds is part of the rolling described just before, not an opposing idea.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Even so" signals something true despite the previous point, but nothing in the text works against the scattering of seeds.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: In Stone Town, the old center of Zanzibar City in Tanzania, many houses have large wooden doors carved with chains, vines, and fish. The size of a door and the richness of its carving once told passersby how wealthy the family inside was. ______ the rows of pointed brass studs on many doors, a style borrowed from India, showed that the owner traded across the Indian Ocean.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Likewise,
choices.B: Nevertheless,
choices.C: Instead,
choices.D: Consequently,

explanation.why: The second sentence says that one feature of a door, its carving, gave passersby information about the family. The last sentence says that another feature, the brass studs, also gave information. A transition that introduces a second, similar point is needed.
explanation.A: Correct. "Likewise" shows that the brass studs, like the carvings, told passersby something about the family.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Nevertheless" signals a contrast, but the studs sent a message just as the carvings did.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Instead" would mean the studs replaced the carvings as a signal, but the text presents both as signals on the same doors.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The brass studs are not a result of the carvings showing wealth; they are another feature that sent a message of their own.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: On Lake Titicaca, high in the Andes between Peru and Bolivia, the Uros people live on islands they have built themselves from thick layers of a reed called totora. The reeds float, but the bottom layers, which sit in the water, slowly rot and fall away. ______ the islanders must keep adding fresh reeds on top, a chore that is repeated every few weeks so that the island does not sink.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Similarly,
choices.B: However,
choices.C: For this reason,
choices.D: For example,

explanation.why: The second sentence explains a problem: the bottom layers of reeds rot and fall away. The last sentence describes what the islanders do about it: they keep adding new reeds. A transition that shows the action taken because of the problem is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Similarly" signals a parallel idea, but adding reeds is the solution to the rotting, not another case of it.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "However" signals a contrast, but adding reeds follows from the rotting rather than contrasting with it.
explanation.C: Correct. "For this reason" shows that the islanders add new reeds because the lower layers rot away.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Adding fresh reeds is not an example of the bottom layers rotting; it is the response to the rotting.

items.subject: literature
items.passage: Nadia and her cousin Leo had planned to spend the first morning of the holiday swimming off the rocks below their grandparents' house. When they reached the water, though, a cold wind had come in overnight, and the waves were gray and rough. ______ they spent the morning walking the tide line, filling their pockets with pieces of sea glass that the waves had worn smooth and cloudy.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Instead,
choices.B: For example,
choices.C: Likewise,
choices.D: Meanwhile,

explanation.why: The first sentence states the cousins' plan: to swim. The second sentence explains why the plan failed. The last sentence describes what they did in place of swimming. A transition that introduces a replacement for the original plan is needed.
explanation.A: Correct. "Instead" shows that collecting sea glass replaced the swim the cousins had planned.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Collecting sea glass is not an example of the rough sea; it is what the cousins did because they could not swim.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Likewise" signals a matching idea, but walking the beach is a different activity from the swim they had planned.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Meanwhile" means at the same time, but the walk replaced the swim rather than happening alongside it.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: During the Onam festival in Kerala, in southern India, villages race long, narrow boats known as snake boats along the backwaters. The largest boats are more than 30 meters long and carry around a hundred rowers, who must pull their paddles in perfect time. ______ each boat carries singers who chant traditional boat songs, setting the rhythm that keeps the rowers' strokes together.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: By contrast,
choices.B: In other words,
choices.C: Consequently,
choices.D: In addition,

explanation.why: The second sentence describes the boats' size and their rowers. The last sentence adds another group of people the boats carry, the singers. A transition that adds a further point is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "By contrast" signals a difference, but the singers work together with the rowers rather than contrasting with them.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "In other words" would restate the previous sentence, but the singers are new information.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The boats do not carry singers because they are long and carry many rowers; the last sentence adds a detail rather than stating a result.
explanation.D: Correct. "In addition" adds the singers to the description of the boats' size and rowers.

items.subject: science
items.passage: The shiny inner layer of many seashells, called nacre or mother-of-pearl, is made almost entirely of a mineral called aragonite. On its own, aragonite is brittle and shatters easily. ______ nacre is remarkably tough, because the mineral is arranged in thousands of tiny flat plates held together by thin layers of soft protein, like bricks in a wall of mortar, so that a crack cannot travel straight through it.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Therefore,
choices.B: Similarly,
choices.C: However,
choices.D: For example,

explanation.why: The second sentence says the mineral aragonite "is brittle and shatters easily." The last sentence says that nacre, made of that mineral, is "remarkably tough." A transition that signals a contrast between the brittle mineral and the tough shell layer is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Therefore" would mean nacre is tough because aragonite is brittle, but the text says the toughness comes from the arrangement of plates, in spite of the brittle mineral.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Similarly" signals a matching quality, but tough and brittle are opposite qualities.
explanation.C: Correct. "However" signals the contrast between the brittle mineral and the tough material it forms when arranged in plates.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Nacre being tough is not an example of aragonite being brittle; it is the opposite.

items.subject: science
items.passage: In the 1950s, the geologist Marie Tharp set out to map the floor of the Atlantic Ocean, but at the time women were not permitted aboard the research ships that measured ocean depths. ______ she worked on land, turning the long lists of depth readings that her colleagues sent back from each voyage into detailed profiles of the seabed. As the profiles accumulated, she noticed a deep valley running down the center of the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, a feature that later proved crucial to the theory of plate tectonics.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: In addition,
choices.B: For instance,
choices.C: Instead,
choices.D: Nevertheless,

explanation.why: The first sentence says Tharp could not go to sea to gather depth readings. The second sentence describes what she did in place of going to sea: she worked on land with readings others collected. A transition that introduces an alternative to the thing that was not possible is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "In addition" would add working on land to going to sea, but the text says she could not go to sea at all.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Working on land is not an example of women being kept off the ships; it is Tharp's response to that rule.
explanation.C: Correct. "Instead" shows that, since she could not work at sea, Tharp did her mapping on land with readings sent to her.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Nevertheless" is tempting because Tharp overcame an obstacle, but the sentence does not say she went to sea despite the ban; it describes the different method she used in its place.

items.subject: science
items.passage: The horned lizards of the deserts of North America rely on several lines of defense. Their flattened bodies and mottled, sandy coloring make them hard to spot among stones and dry grass. If a predator finds one anyway, the lizard puffs itself up and tilts its crown of spines toward the attacker, making itself look larger and harder to swallow. ______ when a coyote or fox persists, some species can squirt a thin stream of blood from the corners of their eyes, a fluid that tastes so foul to these animals that they usually drop the lizard and leave.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Instead,
choices.B: For example,
choices.C: Similarly,
choices.D: Finally,

explanation.why: The text presents the lizard's defenses in the order in which they are used: first camouflage, then puffing up, and last, when the others fail, squirting blood. A transition that introduces the last step in this sequence is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Instead" would mean squirting blood replaces the other defenses, but the text says it comes after they have been tried, when a predator "persists."
explanation.B: Incorrect. Squirting blood is not an example of puffing up and showing spines; it is a separate, later defense.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Similarly" signals a defense like the one just described, but squirting blood is a different kind of defense used only when the earlier ones fail.
explanation.D: Correct. "Finally" marks squirting blood as the last of the several defenses the text lists.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: Many parents have been told that playing Mozart to young children will make them smarter, an idea often called the "Mozart effect." ______ a study published in 1993 did find that college students performed slightly better on a spatial reasoning task after listening to a Mozart sonata than after sitting in silence. But the improvement lasted only about fifteen minutes, the study tested neither infants nor general intelligence, and later research suggested that any upbeat, enjoyable music produced a similar short-term boost.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Similarly,
choices.B: Granted,
choices.C: In fact,
choices.D: Consequently,

explanation.why: The author's point is that the popular claim about the "Mozart effect" goes far beyond the evidence. The blank sentence admits that a real study found a small effect, and the next sentence, beginning with "But," explains why that finding does not support the popular claim. A transition that concedes a point before the author argues against it is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Similarly" signals a parallel idea, but the study's modest finding is being contrasted with the sweeping popular claim, not compared to it.
explanation.B: Correct. "Granted" acknowledges the 1993 finding before the author explains its limits in the following sentence.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "In fact" would present the study as confirming or strengthening the popular claim, but the author goes on to show that the study supports much less than the claim. This is the closest near miss.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The 1993 study was not caused by parents being told about the Mozart effect; the sentence introduces evidence, not a result.

items.subject: science
items.passage: A widely repeated story holds that when lemmings become too numerous, they march to the sea and throw themselves off cliffs. The scene that fixed this image in the public mind, in a 1958 nature documentary, was staged: the animals were pushed into the water by the film crew. ______ the legend grew from a grain of truth. Lemming populations in the Arctic rise and crash in cycles of a few years, and in crowded years large numbers of the animals migrate in search of food, some drowning as they try to cross rivers and lakes.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Therefore,
choices.B: Nevertheless,
choices.C: For example,
choices.D: In other words,

explanation.why: The second sentence shows that the famous footage was faked, which seems to dismiss the story completely. The third sentence says that the story nonetheless has some basis in real lemming behavior. A transition that signals something true in spite of the previous point is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Therefore" would mean the grain of truth follows from the footage being staged, but the two points pull in opposite directions.
explanation.B: Correct. "Nevertheless" shows that, even though the famous scene was staged, the legend has a real basis in lemming migrations.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The grain of truth is not an example of the staged scene; it is a point that partly qualifies the dismissal of the story.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "In other words" would restate the previous sentence, but the third sentence makes a different point: that the story is not entirely false.

items.subject: literature
items.passage: Zainab's uncle sold embroidered cloth from a narrow stall in Anarkali Bazaar in Lahore, and that summer he asked her to help him with the foreign visitors who stopped to look. On her first afternoon, a couple from Germany asked to see a particular shade of blue, and her uncle vanished into the storeroom at the back to search through his bolts of fabric. ______ Zainab was left alone at the counter, answering questions about stitches and dyes that she had never thought to ask him herself, in an English she had used only in class.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: For example,
choices.B: Afterward,
choices.C: Meanwhile,
choices.D: In contrast,

explanation.why: The second sentence describes the uncle going into the storeroom to search. The last sentence describes what Zainab did during that same time, while he was gone. A transition that signals two things happening at the same time is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Zainab answering questions is not an example of her uncle searching for fabric; it is a separate event happening at the same time.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Afterward" is tempting because the text moves from one event to the next, but Zainab is at the counter while her uncle is still searching, not after he returns.
explanation.C: Correct. "Meanwhile" shows that Zainab handled the customers at the same time as her uncle searched the storeroom.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "In contrast" signals opposing ideas, but the uncle searching and Zainab answering questions are not opposites; they happen at once.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: Along the northeastern coast of Japan stand hundreds of stone markers, some of them centuries old, that record the great tsunamis of the past. Most of the stones simply note the date of a wave and the losses it caused, serving as memorials. ______ the stone above the village of Aneyoshi gives a direct instruction, warning residents not to build their homes below the point where it stands. The village's families had obeyed, and when the tsunami of March 2011 swept up the valley, the water stopped just short of the stone.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: As a result,
choices.B: For example,
choices.C: Likewise,
choices.D: By contrast,

explanation.why: The second sentence describes what most stones do: record dates and losses as memorials. The third sentence describes a stone that does something different: it gives an instruction. A transition that signals a difference from the general pattern is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The Aneyoshi stone's instruction is not a result of other stones being memorials.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "For example" is tempting because the Aneyoshi stone is a specific stone, but it is not an example of a memorial that records a date; it does something different.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Likewise" signals a similar case, but the Aneyoshi stone differs from the memorial stones by giving an instruction.
explanation.D: Correct. "By contrast" shows that the Aneyoshi stone, unlike most of the markers, gives a warning rather than a memorial.

items.subject: science
items.passage: Two different creatures are commonly called daddy longlegs, and both are said to carry a venom so powerful that only their tiny mouthparts keep them from being dangerous to people. The claim fails for the first creature, the harvestman, at the outset: harvestmen are not spiders and have no venom glands at all. The second, the cellar spider, does produce venom and uses it to subdue insects. ______ tests in which cellar spiders were induced to bite people produced nothing worse than a brief, mild sting.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Therefore,
choices.B: In fact,
choices.C: Still,
choices.D: Similarly,

explanation.why: The author is arguing against the claim that daddy longlegs are dangerously venomous. The third sentence admits a point in the claim's favor: cellar spiders do have venom. The last sentence returns to the author's position by showing that the venom is harmless to people. A transition that signals a return to the main point after a concession is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Therefore" would mean the mild results follow from the spider having venom, but the harmless bite runs against what the venom claim predicts.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "In fact" would strengthen the point that cellar spiders have venom, but the last sentence works against the idea that the venom is dangerous. This is the closest near miss.
explanation.C: Correct. "Still" shows that, although cellar spiders do have venom, the tests support the author's point that they are harmless to people.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Similarly" signals a parallel point, but a harmless bite is not similar to having venom that subdues prey; it limits that point.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: Kolkata, in eastern India, has the oldest tram system still operating in Asia. Horse-drawn trams began running there in 1873, and electric trams followed in 1902. Supporters of the system point out that the trams produce no exhaust, cost riders very little, and carry far more people per vehicle than cars do. ______ the network has shrunk steadily for decades, as routes were closed to make room for buses and cars on the city's crowded roads, and only a handful of lines now remain in service.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: In other words,
choices.B: Consequently,
choices.C: Nonetheless,
choices.D: For instance,

explanation.why: The third sentence lists the trams' advantages, which would seem to argue for keeping them. The last sentence says the network has been shrinking anyway. A transition that signals a development that goes against what the previous sentence would lead you to expect is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "In other words" would restate the trams' advantages, but the last sentence describes something quite different: the system's decline.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Consequently" is tempting because the sentence describes a change over time, but the shrinking did not result from the trams' advantages; it happened in spite of them.
explanation.C: Correct. "Nonetheless" shows that the network has shrunk despite the advantages its supporters point out.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The shrinking of the network is not an example of the trams' advantages.

items.subject: science
items.passage: Cork, the material used to seal wine bottles and to make floor tiles, is the thick outer bark of the cork oak, a tree grown mainly in Portugal and Spain. Harvesting cork does not require cutting the tree down. Workers strip the bark by hand once every nine years or so, and the tree grows a new layer, so a single oak can be harvested a dozen times over its long life. ______ the open cork oak woodlands, with their widely spaced trees and sunlit grassland, provide habitat for lynx, eagles, and many other species.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Consequently,
choices.B: Furthermore,
choices.C: In contrast,
choices.D: For example,

explanation.why: The second and third sentences describe one benefit of cork harvesting: it does not harm the tree. The last sentence describes a second benefit: the woodlands provide habitat. A transition that adds another point of the same kind is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Consequently" is tempting because the text moves from the harvest to the woodlands, but the habitat the woodlands provide is not a result of the bark regrowing; it is a second, separate benefit.
explanation.B: Correct. "Furthermore" adds the woodlands' value as habitat to the benefit already described.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "In contrast" signals a difference, but providing habitat is another benefit, not a point that opposes the first one.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Providing habitat for lynx and eagles is not an example of harvesting bark without cutting the tree; it is a separate benefit.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: The Hawa Mahal in Jaipur, India, completed in 1799, is a five-story facade of pink sandstone pierced by more than nine hundred small windows. The windows were screened with carved stone lattices so that the women of the royal household, who at the time did not appear in public, could watch festivals and processions in the street below without being seen. The same lattices let the breeze pass freely through the building's narrow upper rooms, keeping them cool through Jaipur's long, hot summers. ______ the building came to be known by the name it carries today, which means "Palace of the Winds."
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Nevertheless,
choices.B: Hence,
choices.C: Likewise,
choices.D: For example,

explanation.why: The third sentence explains that the lattices let the breeze flow through the rooms. The last sentence says the building was named "Palace of the Winds." The name follows from the breeze that moves through the building, so a cause-and-effect transition is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Nevertheless" signals a contrast, but the name agrees with the description of the breezy rooms rather than going against it.
explanation.B: Correct. "Hence" shows that the building was named for the winds because the lattices let the breeze pass through it.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Likewise" would introduce a feature similar to the breeze, but the sentence explains the origin of the name.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The name is not an example of the lattices letting the breeze through; it is a result of that feature.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: The Latin word vomitorium is often explained, in jokes and even in some older reference books, as the name of a room where wealthy Romans emptied their stomachs between courses so that they could go on feasting. No such rooms existed, and no Roman writer describes one. ______ a vomitorium was a passageway in a theater or amphitheater through which crowds poured out at the end of a performance; the word comes from the same root as "vomit" only because the building seemed to spew its audience into the street.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: For example,
choices.B: In other words,
choices.C: Consequently,
choices.D: Rather,

explanation.why: The second sentence rejects the popular explanation of the word. The third sentence gives the correct meaning in its place. A transition that replaces a rejected idea with the right one is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The passageway is not an example of a room that never existed; it is the correct meaning that replaces that idea.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "In other words" is tempting because the sentence explains the word, but it does not restate the previous sentence; it gives a different meaning after the previous one was rejected.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Consequently" would mean the real meaning follows from the fact that no such rooms existed, but the real meaning is a separate fact, not a result.
explanation.D: Correct. "Rather" introduces the true meaning of vomitorium in place of the false one the author has just rejected.

items.subject: literature
items.passage: The regatta was the first race in which Daniel would sit in the stroke seat, setting the pace for the seven rowers behind him. His coach had warned him that the first ten strokes would feel hopeless, as if the oar were catching nothing but air, and that the rhythm would come only if he refused to rush. ______ for the first stretch of the course the boat felt heavy and slow, and Daniel had to fight the urge to shorten his strokes; then, almost without his noticing, the oars began to bite and the boat settled into its run.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: However,
choices.B: Instead,
choices.C: In addition,
choices.D: Indeed,

explanation.why: The second sentence reports the coach's prediction: the first strokes would feel hopeless, and the rhythm would come later. The last sentence describes the race going exactly as predicted. A transition that confirms that the prediction came true is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "However" would mean the race went differently from the coach's warning, but it went just as he said. This is the closest near miss, since the sentence also contains a turn marked by "then."
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Instead" would mean something replaced the predicted experience, but the predicted experience is exactly what Daniel had.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "In addition" would add a new point to the coach's warning, but the sentence describes the race, which bears out the warning rather than adding to it.
explanation.D: Correct. "Indeed" confirms that the coach's warning proved accurate: the boat felt heavy at first, and the rhythm came later.

items.subject: science
items.passage: Most octopuses avoid predators by hiding: they match the color and texture of nearby rocks or coral and stay still until the danger passes. The mimic octopus, which lives on open sandy seafloors off Indonesia, takes a bolder approach, impersonating animals that predators prefer to leave alone. ______ when threatened, it may spread its arms into the banded, spiny outline of a lionfish, or bury six arms in the sand and wave the other two like a pair of venomous sea snakes.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: For instance,
choices.B: Nevertheless,
choices.C: In contrast,
choices.D: As a result,

explanation.why: The second sentence makes a general claim: the mimic octopus impersonates "animals that predators prefer to leave alone." The last sentence describes two particular impersonations, a lionfish and sea snakes, which illustrate that claim. A transition that introduces examples is needed.
explanation.A: Correct. "For instance" introduces the lionfish and sea snake displays as specific cases of the octopus impersonating dangerous animals.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The lionfish and sea snake displays support the claim about impersonation; they do not happen in spite of it.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The contrast in the text is between hiding and impersonating, and that contrast was already made in the second sentence. The last sentence does not contrast with the sentence before it; it illustrates it. This is the most tempting trap.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The specific displays are not caused by the general strategy; they are examples of it.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: Karachi's tramway opened in 1885, and its first cars were pulled by small steam engines running on rails laid along the city's streets. Residents soon complained that the engines were noisy and frightened horses, and within a few years the steam cars had been withdrawn in favor of trams drawn by horses. ______ the system kept growing: new lines spread through the city, and the trams stayed in service, later powered by gasoline engines, until 1975.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Therefore,
choices.B: For example,
choices.C: In other words,
choices.D: Nevertheless,

explanation.why: The second sentence describes a setback: the steam engines caused complaints and had to be withdrawn. The last sentence says the system kept growing anyway, with new lines and ninety years of service. A transition that signals something happened in spite of the setback is needed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Therefore" would mean the complaints caused the system to grow, but the text presents the growth as happening despite the setback, not because of it. This is tempting because the sentence before does describe a cause and an effect.
explanation.B: Incorrect. New lines and long service are not an example of the complaints or the withdrawal.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The growth of the system does not restate the withdrawal of the steam cars; it is a different and contrasting development.
explanation.D: Correct. "Nevertheless" shows that the tramway continued to grow despite the trouble with the steam engines.

items.subject: literature
items.passage: Over the winter, Tomas and his younger brother Luis set out to build a telescope from a secondhand kit, grinding the mirror by hand with abrasive powder and water. The instructions promised a finished mirror after forty hours of work. ______ after sixty hours the glass still showed the faint scratches that the final polish was supposed to remove, and Luis began to ask whether a telescope from a shop would have been simpler. Tomas kept grinding, convinced that one more evening would do it.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Yet,
choices.B: Similarly,
choices.C: For example,
choices.D: In addition,

explanation.why: The second sentence sets an expectation: the instructions "promised a finished mirror after forty hours." The next sentence reports what actually happened: after sixty hours the mirror was still scratched. The transition must signal that reality went against the promise.
