explanation.why: The text says the water "can burn the skin of most animals" and "few creatures can survive there." What keeps other animals away is how hostile the lake is, so the blank needs "harshness."
explanation.A: Correct. The lake's harsh conditions, water that burns skin, keep predators away, and that same harshness protects the flamingos' chicks.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text describes the water as salty and alkaline, not hot.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text says "few creatures can survive there," so wildlife is not what keeps other animals away.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The nests are far out in the lake, but what keeps other animals away, according to the text, is the burning water, not how far away the islands are.

items.subject: science
items.passage: Ambergris is a waxy substance that forms in the digestive system of some sperm whales. When it is first expelled into the sea, it is dark and has an unpleasant smell. After floating in salt water and sunlight for years, however, it hardens, turns pale, and develops a sweet, earthy scent. Perfume makers once prized this ______ ambergris, which could make other fragrances last longer on the skin.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: fresh
choices.B: aged
choices.C: ordinary
choices.D: hidden

explanation.why: The text contrasts newly expelled ambergris, which is "dark" with "an unpleasant smell," with ambergris that has floated "for years" and developed "a sweet, earthy scent." Perfume makers wanted the second kind, so the blank needs "aged."
explanation.A: Incorrect. Fresh ambergris is the dark, bad-smelling kind; perfume makers prized the kind that had changed after years at sea.
explanation.B: Correct. Ambergris that has floated for years, or aged, develops the sweet scent that perfume makers wanted.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Something that perfume makers "prized" is valued, not ordinary.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Nothing in the text says the ambergris was concealed.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: The Pharos of Alexandria, a lighthouse built in Egypt in the third century BCE, stood more than 100 meters tall and was among the tallest structures of the ancient world. A fire burned at its top each night, and its light is said to have been visible far out at sea. The tower was so famous that in several languages the word for lighthouse still ______ its name.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: competes with
choices.B: derives from
choices.C: accounts for
choices.D: substitutes for

explanation.why: The sentence explains a result of the tower being "so famous": the word for lighthouse in several languages still comes from the name Pharos. The blank needs "derives from."
explanation.A: Incorrect. A word and a name do not compete; the sentence is about where the word came from.
explanation.B: Correct. Because the tower was so famous, its name became the word for lighthouse in several languages; those words derive from, or come from, "Pharos."
explanation.C: Incorrect. The word for lighthouse does not explain the tower's name. It is the tower's fame that explains the word.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The tower's name was not replaced by the word for lighthouse; rather, the word grew out of the name.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: In 1905, a librarian in Washington County, Maryland, loaded shelves of books onto a horse-drawn wagon and sent it along the county's back roads. Farming families who lived too far from town to visit the library could now borrow books at their own gates. The wagon was so well received that it ______ many similar services: by the 1920s, motor trucks fitted with shelves were carrying books to rural readers across the United States.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: inspired
choices.B: outlasted
choices.C: delayed
choices.D: replaced

explanation.why: The wagon "was so well received" that other services like it appeared later, as the colon explains. A success that leads others to copy it inspires them, so "inspired" fits.
explanation.A: Correct. Because the wagon was popular, many similar services followed; it inspired them.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text says nothing about how long the wagon lasted compared with the later trucks.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The wagon's success led to more services, not fewer or later ones.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The wagon came first; the similar services came after it, so it could not have replaced them.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: Along the southern coast of Sri Lanka, near the town of Galle, some fishermen work from wooden poles planted in the shallow sea just offshore. Each man climbs his pole at dawn, settles on a crossbar barely wide enough to sit on, and casts a line into the water below. The method requires no boat and no fuel, but it demands remarkable ______: a fisherman may stay perched above the waves for hours without moving.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: strength
choices.B: patience
choices.C: speed
choices.D: courage

explanation.why: The colon explains the blank: a fisherman "may stay perched above the waves for hours without moving." Waiting a long time without moving calls for patience.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Climbing the pole might take some strength, but the sentence after the colon is about waiting for hours, not about physical power.
explanation.B: Correct. Sitting still for hours while waiting for fish requires patience, which is exactly what the colon describes.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Staying still for hours is the opposite of acting quickly.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text does not describe the work as frightening or dangerous; it stresses the long, motionless wait.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: Quetta, the capital of Balochistan province in Pakistan, sits in a high valley where winters are long and cold. The orchards around the city produce apples, apricots, and almonds in summer, but little grows once the snow arrives. For generations, families have therefore dried part of each harvest in the sun. These dried fruits and nuts ______ households through the months when fresh produce is scarce.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: sustain
choices.B: surprise
choices.C: preserve
choices.D: entertain

explanation.why: Families dry part of the harvest because "little grows once the snow arrives." The dried food feeds them during the months when fresh produce is scarce, so the blank needs "sustain," meaning keep going or support.
explanation.A: Correct. The dried fruits and nuts keep households supplied with food, or sustain them, through the winter months.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Nothing in the text suggests the winter food is unexpected; families prepare it on purpose every year.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Drying preserves the fruit, but the sentence is about what the fruit does for the households. People are not preserved; they are fed.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The dried food is stored to be eaten, not to amuse anyone.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: In the 1860s, the first tea of each season to reach London from China sold for the highest prices, so fast sailing ships known as clippers raced one another across half the world. In the famous race of 1866, two clippers that had left China on the same day arrived in the River Thames within hours of each other after a voyage of ninety-nine days, a result so close that it was almost ______.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: a mystery
choices.B: a tie
choices.C: a record
choices.D: a defeat

explanation.why: Two ships that left on the same day "arrived ... within hours of each other" after ninety-nine days at sea. A finish that close is nearly a tie, so "a tie" fits.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Nothing about the result is unexplained; the text tells you exactly what happened.
explanation.B: Correct. After more than three months of racing, the two ships finished within hours of each other, which is almost a tie.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text does not say the voyage was the fastest ever; it says the two ships finished nearly together.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The sentence is about how close the finish was, not about either ship losing.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: Between 1892 and 1954, most immigrants who arrived in New York by ship were taken first to Ellis Island. There, doctors checked each newcomer for illness, and officials asked a list of questions about work, money, and family. The process sounds daunting, but for the great majority it was ______: most people passed through the building in a few hours, and only about two in every hundred were turned away.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: brief
choices.B: permanent
choices.C: exhausting
choices.D: pointless

explanation.why: "But" contrasts the blank with "daunting," and the colon explains it: most people "passed through the building in a few hours." A process that took only a few hours was brief.
explanation.A: Correct. Most immigrants were through in a few hours, so for them the process was brief.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text describes a process that lasted a few hours, not something lasting.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "But" signals that the process was not as hard as it sounds; calling it exhausting would agree with "daunting" instead of contrasting with it.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text says the checks had a purpose and that some people were turned away; it never suggests the process was useless.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: Shisha embroidery, practiced in Sindh in Pakistan and in Gujarat and Rajasthan in India, fixes small pieces of mirror onto cloth. The embroiderer does not glue the glass in place. Instead, each piece is laid on the fabric and a tight ring of thread is stitched around its edge, so that the thread alone ______ the mirror. Light bouncing off dozens of these tiny mirrors makes a finished garment glitter as its wearer moves.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: colors
choices.B: hides
choices.C: polishes
choices.D: secures

explanation.why: The embroiderer "does not glue the glass in place"; instead, a ring of thread is stitched around each piece. The thread therefore does the job the glue would have done, which is holding the mirror in place. "Secures" fits.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text says nothing about the thread changing the color of the mirror.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The mirrors are meant to be seen; the finished garment glitters because light bounces off them.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Thread stitched around the edge of a mirror does not make its surface shiny; the text is about holding the mirror on the cloth.
explanation.D: Correct. Since no glue is used, the ring of thread is what holds, or secures, each mirror on the cloth.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: In Patan, a historic city in Nepal's Kathmandu Valley, many old brick houses have wooden windows carved by Newar craftsmen. A single window frame may be covered with flowers, birds, and twisting vines cut so finely that the wood looks like lace. Because the carving on every house is different, a walk down one narrow street can reveal dozens of ______ designs.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: ancient
choices.B: simple
choices.C: distinct
choices.D: practical

explanation.why: The last sentence gives the reason first: "the carving on every house is different." So a street shows dozens of designs that differ from one another, which is what "distinct" means.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The houses are described as old, but the sentence explains that the designs differ from house to house, not how old they are.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Carving "so finely that the wood looks like lace" is the opposite of simple.
explanation.C: Correct. Because every house's carving is different, the designs along a street are distinct from one another.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text describes the carvings as decorative, like lace; nothing suggests they are useful rather than beautiful.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: Batik, a method of decorating cloth that is especially associated with the Indonesian island of Java, depends on wax. Using a small copper tool with a spout, the artist draws lines of hot wax onto plain fabric. When the cloth is dipped in dye, the waxed areas ______ the color, so they remain pale while the rest of the cloth darkens. Boiling the cloth afterward removes the wax and reveals the pattern.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: repel
choices.B: absorb
choices.C: brighten
choices.D: spread

explanation.why: The waxed areas "remain pale while the rest of the cloth darkens," so the wax must keep the dye out. A word meaning "keep away" is needed, and "repel" fits.
explanation.A: Correct. The wax keeps the dye from reaching the cloth, so the waxed areas repel the color and stay pale.
explanation.B: Incorrect. If the waxed areas absorbed the dye, they would darken like the rest of the cloth instead of staying pale.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The waxed areas stay pale because the dye does not reach them, not because they make the color stronger.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The waxed lines hold the dye back; they do not carry it farther across the cloth.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: In many West African societies, a griot is a storyteller, musician, and historian rolled into one. For centuries, before most local histories were written down, griots memorized the names of rulers, the details of battles, and the family lines of whole communities, and they passed this knowledge on to their children. A griot's songs were therefore not just entertainment; they were a community's living ______.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: language
choices.B: archive
choices.C: performance
choices.D: celebration

explanation.why: Griots memorized rulers' names, battles, and family lines at a time "before most local histories were written down." Their songs stored a community's records, so the blank needs "archive," a collection of records.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text does not say the songs were a language; it says they preserved historical knowledge.
explanation.B: Correct. The songs held a community's history the way written records would, so they were a living archive.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Not just entertainment" tells you the blank must be something beyond a show, and a performance is still a kind of entertainment.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The songs did more than celebrate; the text stresses that they stored names, dates, and family lines.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: Whaling voyages in the 1800s could last three years or more, and sailors had long stretches of empty time between hunts. Many filled the hours with scrimshaw: they scratched pictures of ships, whales, and faraway ports into whale teeth with a sailmaker's needle, then rubbed soot or ink into the lines to make the images stand out. Though the sailors rarely had any art training, some of their carvings are remarkably ______, with details as fine as a pen drawing.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: large
choices.B: valuable
choices.C: skillful
choices.D: plain

explanation.why: "Though" sets up a contrast with "rarely had any art training," and the phrase after the comma describes "details as fine as a pen drawing." Untrained sailors producing such fine work is surprising skill, so "skillful" fits.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Whale teeth are small, and the text is about the fine detail of the carvings, not their size.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text says nothing about what the carvings were worth; it describes how well they were made.
explanation.C: Correct. Despite having no training, the sailors produced carvings with fine detail, which shows skill.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Details "as fine as a pen drawing" are the opposite of plain.

items.subject: literature
items.passage: When the chain slipped off Amir's bicycle for the third time, he was ready to give up on the bike. His neighbor Mr. Okafor came over with a toolbox but did not fix the chain himself. Instead, he handed Amir a wrench, pointed to the rear wheel, and answered each of Amir's questions with another question. By sunset the chain was tight, and Amir had done every step with his own hands. Mr. Okafor had not come to fix a bicycle, Amir realized; he had come to give ______.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: an apology
choices.B: a warning
choices.C: a lesson
choices.D: a demonstration

explanation.why: Mr. Okafor "did not fix the chain himself" but made Amir do "every step with his own hands," answering questions with questions. He was teaching Amir to fix the bike himself, so what he came to give was a lesson.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Mr. Okafor has done nothing wrong and has no reason to apologize.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Mr. Okafor does not caution Amir about anything; he guides him through the repair.
explanation.C: Correct. By making Amir do the work and guiding him with questions, Mr. Okafor taught him how to fix the chain; he came to give a lesson.
explanation.D: Incorrect. A demonstration would mean showing Amir how to do the repair, but Mr. Okafor "did not fix the chain himself"; he made Amir do every step.

items.subject: literature
items.passage: All afternoon the sky over Karachi had been the color of wet cement, and Hira and her younger sister Zoya sat on the rooftop, waiting. Twice Zoya held out her palm and announced a raindrop; twice it was nothing. When the first real drops finally struck the hot concrete and the smell of dust rose around them, the girls' long wait turned at once into ______: they leaped up, shouting, and spun in circles until their clothes were soaked.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: disappointment
choices.B: delight
choices.C: confusion
choices.D: silence

explanation.why: The colon explains the blank: the girls "leaped up, shouting, and spun in circles" when the rain came. That is joyful behavior, so the long wait turned into delight.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The rain is what the girls wanted, and they celebrate when it comes, so they are not disappointed.
explanation.B: Correct. Leaping, shouting, and spinning in the rain show that the girls were overjoyed; their waiting turned into delight.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The girls know exactly what has happened: the rain they were waiting for has arrived.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The girls are shouting, the opposite of silence.

items.subject: literature
items.passage: For the first week at her new school, Mei said almost nothing. She chose the seat nearest the window, answered questions in a voice the teacher could barely hear, and spent lunch reading alone. Her classmates decided she was shy and left her alone. They were wrong. Mei was not timid; she was ______, taking careful note of who was kind, who was loud, and whom she might like to know before deciding where to begin.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: lonely
choices.B: observant
choices.C: nervous
choices.D: bored

explanation.why: The text says the classmates "were wrong" to think Mei was shy, and it explains what she was actually doing: "taking careful note" of everyone around her. Someone who watches carefully is observant.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Mei is alone by choice while she studies her classmates; the text does not say she is unhappy about it.
explanation.B: Correct. Mei is quietly watching and noting who is kind and who is loud, which is what being observant means.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text says Mei "was not timid," so describing her as nervous repeats the mistake her classmates made.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Mei is paying close attention to her classmates, not losing interest in them.

items.subject: literature
items.passage: Tariq had ridden the city bus a hundred times with his mother, but today he rode it alone for the first time. He counted the stops under his breath, checked the name of each street against the folded note in his pocket, and kept one hand on the bell cord the whole way. When the bus finally reached the library and he stepped down onto the curb, his careful ______ had paid off: he had not missed a single turn.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: silence
choices.B: speed
choices.C: attention
choices.D: memory

explanation.why: Tariq counts the stops, checks every street name against his note, and keeps his hand on the bell cord. He is watching closely the whole way, and that close watching is what "paid off." The blank needs "attention."
explanation.A: Incorrect. Tariq is quiet, but being quiet is not what gets him to the right stop; watching the streets and counting the stops does.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Nothing in the text is about going fast; Tariq's success comes from being careful.
explanation.C: Correct. Counting stops and checking street names are ways of paying attention, and that careful attention is why he did not miss a turn.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Tariq does not rely on remembering the route; he checks each street against a written note.

items.subject: literature
items.passage: The storm had brought down the old treehouse, and in the morning Dev and his brother Rohan stood under the oak looking at the pile of splintered boards. Rohan wanted to haul the wreck to the curb and forget about it. Dev had other ideas. He sorted out the boards that could be reused, sketched a new platform on an envelope, and began pulling bent nails out of the wood. Where Rohan saw only a loss, Dev saw ______.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: a mystery
choices.B: a warning
choices.C: a burden
choices.D: an opportunity

explanation.why: The last sentence contrasts the brothers. Rohan wants to throw the wreck away, while Dev sorts usable boards and sketches a new platform. Dev sees a chance to build something new, so the blank needs "an opportunity."
explanation.A: Incorrect. There is nothing puzzling about the wreck; the text says the storm brought it down.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Dev is not treating the fallen treehouse as a danger to avoid; he is planning to build again.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Seeing the wreck as a burden is close to Rohan's view, who wants to be rid of it, not the contrasting view Dev holds.
explanation.D: Correct. Dev starts planning and salvaging materials for a new treehouse, so he sees the wreck as an opportunity.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: In the foothills of central Nepal, Gurung honey hunters harvest the nests of the world's largest honeybee, which builds its combs high on sheer cliff faces. Twice a year, a hunter climbs a rope ladder that hangs from the clifftop, steadies himself far above the ground, and uses a long bamboo pole to cut a comb free while smoke from a fire below calms the bees. The work is dangerous and slow, yet the hunters are careful to leave part of every nest ______, so that the colony survives and the cliff can be harvested again the following season.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: empty
choices.B: intact
choices.C: visible
choices.D: exposed

explanation.why: The hunters leave part of each nest "so that the colony survives" and the cliff "can be harvested again." For the bees to survive, part of the nest must be left unharmed, so "intact" fits.
explanation.A: Incorrect. An empty nest would mean the comb had been taken; the hunters deliberately leave part of it to keep the colony alive.
explanation.B: Correct. Leaving part of the nest intact, that is, whole and undamaged, lets the colony survive and rebuild for the next harvest.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The nests are already on open cliff faces; whether part of a nest can be seen has nothing to do with the colony surviving.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The nests are already exposed on "sheer cliff faces." The hunters' concern is the colony's survival, not leaving the nest open to view.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: Landscape architects use the term "desire path" for a trail worn into the grass where people have repeatedly walked instead of using the paved route nearby. Planners once treated such trails as a nuisance to be fenced off or reseeded. Some now take the opposite view: on new campuses and in parks, they lay out only the main walkways at first, wait a season to see where desire paths appear, and then pave those. In this approach, a trampled strip of lawn is not evidence of carelessness but a form of ______ from the very people the space is meant to serve.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: neglect
choices.B: permission
choices.C: feedback
choices.D: protest

explanation.why: The planners described wait to see where people actually walk and then pave those routes. The worn trails tell them what walkers want, so the trails are a kind of information from users: feedback.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The sentence says the trampled lawn is "not evidence of carelessness," so neglect is the view the text rejects.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Walkers are not granting the planners anything; the paths show the planners what the walkers want.
explanation.C: Correct. The worn paths show planners where people want to walk, which is feedback, and the planners act on it by paving those routes.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The walkers are not objecting to anything; they are simply taking the most convenient route, and the planners read that route as useful information.

items.subject: science
items.passage: In 1927, a physics professor at the University of Queensland in Australia poured heated pitch, a tar-like material, into a glass funnel and left it to settle. Pitch at room temperature seems unmistakably solid; a hammer blow will shatter it into sharp pieces. Yet over the decades the pitch in the funnel has slowly formed drops that stretch, thin, and finally fall into a beaker below, at a rate of roughly one drop every ten years. The experiment demonstrates that the ______ of pitch can be deceiving: a substance that breaks like glass is nevertheless, over long enough stretches of time, a flowing liquid.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: weight
choices.B: temperature
choices.C: appearance
choices.D: age

explanation.why: Pitch "seems unmistakably solid" and shatters like glass, yet it slowly flows. What is deceiving is how the pitch looks and behaves at first glance, so the blank needs "appearance."
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text never discusses how heavy the pitch is.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The pitch's temperature is stated plainly as room temperature and is not misleading; what misleads is that the material seems solid.
explanation.C: Correct. Pitch looks and feels like a solid, but it is really a very slow liquid, so its appearance is deceiving.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The experiment has run for decades, but nothing about the pitch's age is misleading; the point is that a solid-looking material flows.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: In the ninth century, scholars in Baghdad undertook a vast effort to render works of Greek, Persian, and Indian learning into Arabic. Supported by the Abbasid caliphs, translators produced Arabic versions of treatises on geometry, astronomy, and medicine, some of which no longer survive in their original languages. The translators did not treat the older texts as finished authorities. They added commentaries, corrected calculations, and tested claims against their own observations, so that translation became a form of ______ rather than mere copying: the Arabic versions often advanced the fields they inherited.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: imitation
choices.B: inquiry
choices.C: preservation
choices.D: decoration

explanation.why: The translators "corrected calculations" and "tested claims against their own observations," and their versions "advanced the fields." Translation done this way is a kind of investigation, so "inquiry" fits the contrast with "mere copying."
explanation.A: Incorrect. Imitation is another word for copying, which the sentence says the translation was not.
explanation.B: Correct. By questioning, correcting, and testing the older texts, the translators turned translation into inquiry, a form of active investigation.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Preserving texts is close to copying them, but the sentence contrasts the blank with "mere copying" and stresses that the translators changed and tested what they received.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text says nothing about making the texts more beautiful; the translators added commentaries and corrections.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: At the Globe, an open-air playhouse in London, a spectator in the early 1600s could stand in the yard in front of the stage for a penny, while those who paid more sat under cover in the galleries. The standing crowd, nicknamed the groundlings, was close enough to the actors to shout at them, and it did. Historians caution, however, against picturing these playgoers as a mob that came only for sword fights and jokes. The same penny bought them long speeches and intricate plots, and the theater's success suggests that the groundlings were far more ______ than their nickname implies.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: restless
choices.B: numerous
choices.C: wealthy
choices.D: discerning

explanation.why: The historians reject the picture of the groundlings as "a mob that came only for sword fights and jokes" and note that the same audience paid for "long speeches and intricate plots." The blank must credit the groundlings with better judgment than the nickname suggests, so "discerning" fits.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Restlessness fits the picture of a rowdy mob, which is the view the historians warn against.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text is about the quality of the groundlings' taste, not about how many of them there were.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The groundlings paid only a penny, while wealthier spectators sat in the galleries.
explanation.D: Correct. An audience that kept paying for long speeches and complex plots showed good judgment, or discernment, which is what the historians argue.

items.subject: literature
items.passage: When his sons offered to buy him an outboard motor, old Tomás thanked them and went on rowing. They argued that the motor would get him to the fishing grounds in a quarter of the time, and he agreed that it would. But he had rowed the same stretch of bay for fifty years, and he knew the water by the pull of it against the oars: where the current quickened over the sandbar, where the cold spring welled up from the bottom. A motor would have ______ him from all of that. The time saved, he said, was time he did not want.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: distracted
choices.B: freed
choices.C: separated
choices.D: protected

explanation.why: Tomás knows the bay "by the pull of it against the oars." A motor would mean no more rowing, so he would lose that direct contact with the water. The blank needs a word meaning "cut off," and "separated ... from" fits.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The motor would not divert his attention from the water; it would remove the contact through which he feels it.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Freed from" suggests escaping a burden, but Tomás does not want to escape the water; he turns the motor down to keep that contact.
explanation.C: Correct. Without the oars, Tomás would no longer feel the water, so a motor would separate him from the knowledge he prizes.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The currents and cold springs are not dangers Tomás wants protection from; they are things he values knowing.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: The geta bera, the drum that leads Kandyan dance processions in Sri Lanka, is carved from a single block of wood and has a head at each end. The two heads are not ______: traditionally they are made from different animal hides, so that one side gives a sharp, high note and the other a deeper, rounder one. A skilled drummer moves constantly between the two, and the contrast between the voices is what gives the drum its characteristic rhythm.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: visible
choices.B: decorated
choices.C: separate
choices.D: identical

explanation.why: The colon after the blank explains the statement: the heads are made from "different animal hides" and give different notes, and the text stresses "the contrast between the voices." So the blank must say that the two heads are not the same, which is what "identical" means.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Nothing in the text concerns whether the heads can be seen.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text says nothing about decoration; it is about the sound each head makes.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The heads are at opposite ends of the drum, so they clearly are separate; what the colon explains is that they differ from each other.
explanation.D: Correct. The two heads differ in material and sound, so they are not identical.

items.subject: literature
items.passage: On her first day in Mr. Haddad's bindery, Leila tried to fold the signatures the way she folded letters: quickly, with a single sweep of her thumb. He stopped her, took the paper, and showed her how to crease it with the bone folder in one slow, even stroke. For a week she found the pace ______, and she said so. By the second week, though, the folds that had once wrinkled lay flat, and she understood why he had refused to let her hurry.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: soothing
choices.B: effortless
choices.C: mysterious
choices.D: exasperating

explanation.why: Leila wants to work "quickly," and Mr. Haddad forces her to slow down. She complains ("she said so"), and the next sentence begins with "though," signaling a turn from her negative reaction to her later understanding. The blank therefore needs a word for an annoyed reaction to the slow pace, and "exasperating" fits.
explanation.A: Incorrect. A soothing pace would not be something to complain about, and "though" would then make no sense.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The slow, careful stroke is the opposite of effortless for someone used to rushing, and an easy pace would give her nothing to complain about.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The method has been shown to her clearly; her problem is its slowness, not any mystery about it.
explanation.D: Correct. Someone who wants to hurry and is made to go slowly finds the pace exasperating, which explains why she complained.

items.subject: literature
items.passage: The boat had been their father's, and for three summers it had sat upside down behind the shed while the paint flaked away. When Rosa finally proposed repainting it, her sister Marta agreed at once, but their ideas of the job were different. Rosa wanted the hull ______ in a single afternoon: scrape, prime, paint, done. Marta insisted on sanding every plank and letting each coat dry overnight. The work took ten days, and when they turned the boat right side up, even Rosa admitted that the patient way had been the right one.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: preserved
choices.B: finished
choices.C: abandoned
choices.D: inspected

explanation.why: The sisters' "ideas of the job were different": Rosa wants everything done "in a single afternoon: scrape, prime, paint, done," while Marta takes ten days. The blank describes Rosa's goal of completing the whole job quickly, so "finished" is the precise choice.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Preserving the boat is the purpose of repainting it, but the sentence is about how fast Rosa wants the job completed.
explanation.B: Correct. Rosa wants the whole job completed in one afternoon, in contrast to Marta's ten-day approach.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Rosa is the one who proposed repainting the boat; she does not want to give it up.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Rosa's list ("scrape, prime, paint") is a plan for doing the work, not for examining the boat.

items.subject: literature
items.passage: Each Sunday, Tariq's grandfather set up the chessboard on the veranda and said nothing until the game was over. Tariq, who was used to teachers who explained every move, found the silence unsettling at first. He lost, and lost again, and his grandfather only reset the pieces. It was weeks before Tariq realized that the silence was not indifference but ______: his grandfather was leaving him room to notice his own mistakes, which, once noticed, he never repeated.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: impatience
choices.B: restraint
choices.C: disapproval
choices.D: confusion

explanation.why: The sentence contrasts what the silence is not ("indifference") with what it is, and the colon explains: the grandfather is deliberately holding back so that Tariq can find his own mistakes. A deliberate decision not to speak or act is "restraint."
explanation.A: Incorrect. The grandfather calmly resets the pieces week after week; nothing suggests he is impatient.
explanation.B: Correct. The grandfather chooses to hold back his comments on purpose, which is restraint.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The silence is a teaching method that helps Tariq, not a sign that the grandfather disapproves of him.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The grandfather is not confused; he knows exactly what he is doing, as the colon explains.

items.subject: science
items.passage: Pollen grains have a tough outer wall that lets them survive for thousands of years in the mud at the bottom of lakes. By drilling a core through these layered sediments and counting the grains in each layer, researchers can reconstruct how a region's vegetation changed over time. The record is not a simple mirror of the past landscape, however. Wind-pollinated trees such as pine release enormous quantities of pollen, so they are ______ in the core relative to their actual numbers, while insect-pollinated plants, which produce far less, can be nearly invisible.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: overrepresented
choices.B: preserved
choices.C: undercounted
choices.D: concentrated

explanation.why: The text says the record is "not a simple mirror" of the landscape. Pines release "enormous quantities of pollen," and the sentence contrasts them with insect-pollinated plants that are "nearly invisible" in the core. So pines must appear in the core more than their real numbers would justify: they are "overrepresented."
explanation.A: Correct. Because pines shed so much pollen, they show up in the core out of proportion to their actual numbers.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The first sentence says all pollen grains survive in the mud; being preserved does not explain why the record is not a mirror of the landscape.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This reverses the logic: a tree that releases huge amounts of pollen would be counted too often, not too rarely.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Concentrated" describes grains being packed together in one place, not how a species' share of the core compares with its real numbers.

items.subject: science
items.passage: Tree-ring dating works by matching the pattern of wide and narrow rings in a piece of wood against a reference sequence built from thousands of samples. In a good year a tree adds a wide ring; in a drought, a narrow one. Because the sequence of good and bad years in a region is ______, a stretch of forty or fifty rings will usually fit the reference in only one place, fixing the year each ring grew. The method does have a limit: if a beam was trimmed before use, its outermost rings are lost, and the felling date can only be estimated.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: repetitive
choices.B: gradual
choices.C: distinctive
choices.D: predictable

explanation.why: The clause after the blank says a run of rings "will usually fit the reference in only one place." That is possible only if the pattern of good and bad years is unique enough not to be confused with any other stretch of years, so the blank needs a word meaning "unlike any other": "distinctive."
explanation.A: Incorrect. A repeating pattern would fit the reference in many places, which is the opposite of what the sentence says.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text describes sharp year-to-year differences (wide ring, narrow ring), not slow change.
explanation.C: Correct. A distinctive pattern matches the reference in only one position, which is what allows an exact date.
explanation.D: Incorrect. If the sequence of years could be predicted, it would not need matching; the method depends on the pattern being unique, not foreseeable.

items.subject: science
items.passage: The Namib Desert of southwestern Africa receives almost no rain, but on many mornings a thick fog rolls in from the Atlantic. Several darkling beetles that live there have turned this fog into a water supply. At dawn a beetle climbs a dune ridge, faces the wind, and tilts its body so that its back is raised. Droplets ______ on the bumpy surface of its wing cases, merge into larger drops, and roll down grooves toward its mouth. The beetle never visits a pool or a stream; the only water it ever drinks is the water it harvests from the air.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: collect
choices.B: evaporate
choices.C: dissolve
choices.D: scatter

explanation.why: The sentence describes a sequence: droplets do something on the beetle's back, then "merge into larger drops" and "roll down" to its mouth. For the fog to become drinking water, the droplets must first gather on the surface, so "collect" fits.
explanation.A: Correct. Fog droplets gather, or collect, on the beetle's back, then merge and run down to its mouth.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Droplets that evaporated would disappear, not merge and roll to the beetle's mouth.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The droplets are water; there is nothing for them to dissolve into, and dissolving would not produce drinking water.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Scattering would spread the droplets apart, the opposite of what must happen for them to merge.

items.subject: science
items.passage: Common cranes migrating between northern Europe and Spain are large birds, and flapping their broad wings for hours is costly. On long stretches over land, they therefore rely on thermals, columns of warm air rising from sun-heated ground. A flock circles inside one column, gaining height almost without moving its wings, then glides for kilometers to the next. This strategy ______ the energy the birds spend on each day's flight, but it also ties them to the sun: thermals weaken in the evening, so cranes generally land before dusk and wait for the next morning's heat.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: reduces
choices.B: replaces
choices.C: increases
choices.D: measures

explanation.why: Flapping "is costly," and the cranes use thermals to gain height "almost without moving" their wings. The strategy therefore lowers the energy cost of flight, and the "but" that follows introduces its drawback. "Reduces" states the benefit precisely.
explanation.A: Correct. Soaring on thermals instead of flapping lowers the energy spent on each day's flight.
explanation.B: Incorrect. A strategy cannot replace energy; the cranes still spend energy, just less of it.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This reverses the point: the cranes use thermals because flapping is costly, so their method saves energy.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The birds are not measuring anything; the sentence is about how much energy they use.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: Before the seventh century BCE, traders in western Anatolia paid for goods with lumps of electrum, a natural mix of gold and silver, which had to be weighed and tested at every exchange. The kingdom of Lydia changed this by stamping pieces of electrum with a royal mark, which ______ that each piece had a fixed weight and purity. A merchant who accepted a stamped coin no longer needed his own scales, and trade became faster. The idea spread quickly to Greek cities along the coast, and within two centuries coins were used around much of the Mediterranean.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: concealed
choices.B: guaranteed
choices.C: questioned
choices.D: suggested

explanation.why: The result of the royal stamp is that a merchant "no longer needed his own scales." That could be true only if the stamp gave a firm assurance of the coin's weight and purity. "Guaranteed" expresses that assurance.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The stamp made the weight and purity known, not hidden.
explanation.B: Correct. The stamp promised a fixed weight and purity, so merchants could trust a coin without testing it.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The stamp removed doubts about the metal; it did not raise them.
explanation.D: Incorrect. A mark that merely suggested the weight would not have let merchants give up their scales; the text requires a firm assurance.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: Listeners sometimes assume that because jazz musicians improvise, they simply play whatever comes to mind. Musicians themselves describe something quite different. A soloist may invent a melody on the spot, but she does so over chord changes she has practiced for years, drawing on phrases she has absorbed from hundreds of recordings. Far from being ______, improvisation is the product of long preparation: the more thoroughly a player has studied the material, the freer she is to depart from it in performance.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: rehearsed
choices.B: predictable
choices.C: haphazard
choices.D: collaborative

explanation.why: The text rejects the idea that musicians "simply play whatever comes to mind" and insists instead that improvisation is "the product of long preparation." "Far from being" introduces the rejected idea, so the blank needs a word for playing without plan or order: "haphazard."
explanation.A: Incorrect. This reverses the sentence: "far from being rehearsed" would deny the preparation that the text says improvisation depends on.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text does not say improvisation is unpredictable; it says the music is less random than listeners assume.
explanation.C: Correct. The listeners' mistaken idea is that improvisation is random; the text says it rests on years of preparation.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text does not discuss whether players work together; the contrast is between random playing and preparation.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: Large national seed vaults store samples of crop varieties in freezers for the long term, but a growing number of villages and neighborhoods run seed libraries of their own. Members borrow a packet of beans or tomato seeds in spring, grow the plants, and return seeds from the harvest in the fall. The point is not only storage. Because the seeds are planted every year, the varieties keep ______ to local soil and weather, something a frozen sample in a vault cannot do. A bean that has been grown in the same valley for fifty years is, in a small way, a different bean from the one that was first saved.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: appealing
choices.B: contributing
choices.C: returning
choices.D: adapting

explanation.why: The text contrasts seeds that are planted every year with a frozen sample that "cannot" change, and the last sentence says a bean grown in one valley for fifty years becomes "a different bean." The varieties therefore keep changing to suit local conditions, which is "adapting."
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Appealing to" soil and weather makes no sense; the sentence is about change over generations, not attractiveness.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text does not say the plants give anything to the soil; it says they change in response to it.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Members return seeds to the library, but the sentence is about what the varieties do in response to "local soil and weather."
explanation.D: Correct. Planted year after year, the varieties keep adjusting to local conditions, which a frozen sample cannot do.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: Pashmina shawls are woven in the Kashmir Valley from the soft undercoat of goats raised on the high, cold plateaus of Ladakh. Each spring the goats are combed, and the fine fibers are separated from the coarse outer hair. Spinning this fiber is ______ work: a single fiber is thinner than a human hair, and it breaks if it is pulled too hard or too fast. For this reason, much of the yarn is still spun by hand on a wooden wheel by women who learned the skill from their mothers, and a single shawl can take weeks to complete.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: monotonous
choices.B: profitable
choices.C: seasonal
choices.D: delicate

explanation.why: The colon explains the blank: the fiber is "thinner than a human hair" and "breaks if it is pulled too hard or too fast." Work that must be done gently with fragile material is "delicate" work.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text does not say the work is boring; it says the fiber is fragile and must be handled with care.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text never mentions what spinners earn.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The combing of the goats happens "each spring," but nothing says the spinning is limited to one season.
explanation.D: Correct. Spinning a fiber that breaks easily requires gentle, careful handling, which is what "delicate" means.

items.subject: science
items.passage: The Sindhri, a long yellow mango grown in the Sindh province of Pakistan, is prized for its sweetness and low fiber. A grower who wants more trees of this kind cannot simply plant its seeds. A mango seed carries a mix of traits from two parent trees, so a seedling may bear fruit that is smaller, stringier, or less sweet than the fruit it came from. Instead, nurseries ______ a bud or shoot from a proven Sindhri tree onto the rootstock of a hardy seedling. The new tree is, in effect, a continuation of the original, and its fruit is reliably the same.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: transplant
choices.B: graft
choices.C: harvest
choices.D: scatter

explanation.why: "Instead" signals an alternative to planting seeds. The method joins "a bud or shoot" from one tree "onto the rootstock" of another so that the new tree is "a continuation of the original." Joining a shoot onto another plant's roots is grafting.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Transplanting means moving a whole plant to new soil, not attaching part of one plant to another.
explanation.B: Correct. To graft is to attach a bud or shoot from one plant onto the root system of another, which matches "onto the rootstock."
explanation.C: Incorrect. Harvesting means gathering fruit; it does not describe joining a shoot onto a rootstock.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Scattering a shoot makes no sense, and spreading seeds is the method the text has just rejected.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: The arrangement of letters on most English keyboards dates from the 1870s, when the inventor Christopher Latham Sholes was refining his typewriter. A popular story holds that Sholes deliberately scattered common letters in order to slow typists down, since fast typing made the machine's metal arms jam. Some historians are ______ of this account. They point out that the layout also seems designed to keep letters that are often typed in sequence on different arms, a change that would reduce jams without slowing anyone, and that no document from Sholes explains his reasoning.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: protective
choices.B: unaware
choices.C: skeptical
choices.D: convinced

explanation.why: The sentences after the blank raise objections to the popular story: the layout could reduce jams "without slowing anyone," and no document from Sholes supports the story. Historians who raise such doubts are "skeptical" of the account.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The historians are challenging the story, not defending it.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The historians clearly know the account, since they argue against it.
explanation.C: Correct. The historians doubt the popular story and give reasons for their doubt.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Historians who point out problems with the story are not convinced by it.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: For centuries, the economy of Bahrain rested on pearls gathered from oyster beds in the shallow waters of the Gulf. Divers worked without any breathing equipment, wearing a clip on the nose and a stone weight on one foot that carried them quickly to the bottom. Each dive lasted little more than a minute, and a diver might make dozens of descents in a day through the hottest months of the year. The trade did not end because the oysters ran out. In the 1930s, cultured pearls from Japan ______ the market, and prices for natural pearls collapsed.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: monitored
choices.B: abandoned
choices.C: flooded
choices.D: revived

explanation.why: The text explains why the trade ended: cultured pearls did something to the market that made prices for natural pearls collapse. A sudden large supply of a cheaper alternative drives prices down, and that is what "flooded the market" means.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Watching the market would not have caused prices to collapse.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Cultured pearls entered the market in large numbers; they did not leave it.
explanation.C: Correct. Cultured pearls arrived in such quantity that they overwhelmed the market and drove down prices.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Reviving the market would have helped the pearl trade, but the text says prices collapsed and the trade ended.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: In 1699, the artist and naturalist Maria Sibylla Merian sailed from Amsterdam to the Dutch colony of Suriname to study insects in the wild. At the time, European collectors usually drew a butterfly or beetle as a lone specimen, pinned and isolated on a blank page. Merian's plates, published in 1705, were ______ by comparison: each shows an insect at several stages of its life, from egg to caterpillar to adult, on the plant that it feeds on. Her work treated the insect not as an object but as a creature with a history and a home.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: conventional
choices.B: comprehensive
choices.C: ornamental
choices.D: accurate

explanation.why: The contrast is between a "lone specimen" on a blank page and Merian's plates, which show "several stages" of an insect's life together with its food plant. Her plates include far more of the insect's story, so "comprehensive" fits.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The pinned, isolated specimen was the convention; Merian's plates departed from it.
explanation.B: Correct. Showing the whole life cycle and the host plant makes the plates comprehensive compared with a single pinned specimen.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text presents the plates as scientific records of life stages and habitat, not as decoration.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text does not say the earlier drawings were inaccurate; the difference is in how much they include, not how correct they are.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: A carillon is a set of at least twenty-three bells, usually hung in a tower and played from a keyboard of wooden levers that the player strikes with loosely closed fists. Because the bells are fixed in place and only their clappers move, a carillon can be played with far more ______ than church bells swung by rope: the player can sound a quiet note or a loud one, a single bell or a chord, and a rapid run of notes that a ringer pulling on ropes could never manage.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: volume
choices.B: effort
choices.C: tradition
choices.D: control

explanation.why: The colon lists what the carillon player can do: choose "a quiet note or a loud one," one bell or several, fast or slow. All of these are ways of deciding exactly how the bells sound, so the blank must mean command over the music: "control."
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text says the player can choose a quiet note as well as a loud one, so the advantage is not simply loudness.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The point is what the player can do, not how hard the player works; a rope ringer might use more effort and still have fewer options.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text compares what each kind of instrument can do, not how old or traditional each is.
explanation.D: Correct. Fixed bells let the player decide the loudness, combination, and speed of the notes, which is control.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: In the days of the telegraph, every message was tapped out by hand as a series of short and long signals. The code was the same for everyone, yet experienced operators insisted that no two people sent it quite alike. One would leave slightly longer pauses between words; another would clip the long signals short. Operators called this personal style a "fist," and a seasoned listener could often ______ a colleague at a distant station by sound alone, long before the message included a name.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: identify
choices.B: contact
choices.C: correct
choices.D: imitate

explanation.why: Each operator had a recognizable personal style, and the listener could tell who was sending "by sound alone, long before the message included a name." Knowing who someone is from a clue is to "identify" them.
explanation.A: Correct. The personal "fist" let a listener work out which colleague was sending before any name appeared.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Reaching a colleague is not something done "by sound alone"; the sentence is about recognizing who is sending.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Nothing in the text is about fixing mistakes in a colleague's sending.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The sentence is about recognizing another operator, not copying that operator's style.

items.subject: science
items.passage: A beaver dam looks like an obstacle, and for a long time landowners treated it as one, tearing out dams to keep streams flowing. Recent studies in the dry valleys of the western United States suggest the dams do something more useful. The pond behind a dam slows the stream and pushes water into the surrounding soil, raising the water table across the valley floor. When a dry summer arrives, that stored water seeps back out slowly, and the meadow stays green while land along undammed streams turns brown. In effect, the beavers ______ water during wet months for release during dry ones.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: waste
choices.B: bank
choices.C: purify
choices.D: divert

explanation.why: The text says water is "stored" in the soil behind the dam and then "seeps back out slowly" in a dry summer. The last sentence sums this up: the beavers put water aside in wet months and release it later. Setting something aside for later use is to "bank" it.
explanation.A: Incorrect. This reverses the point: the dams save water that would otherwise flow away.
explanation.B: Correct. To bank water is to store it for later, which matches "stored water" released "during dry ones."
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text says nothing about making the water cleaner.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The dam does push water sideways into the soil, but the sentence is about saving water for release later, not merely sending it elsewhere.

items.subject: science
items.passage: Prairie dogs live in large colonies on the grasslands of North America, and when a predator appears, one animal gives a sharp call that sends the others diving into their burrows. Early observers assumed the call was a simple alarm with a single meaning: danger. Field experiments tell a more ______ story. When researchers walked a dog, a coyote, or a hawk past a colony, the calls differed in ways the animals could apparently hear, and the colony's response differed too, with some predators sending the prairie dogs underground and others merely putting them on alert.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: familiar
choices.B: troubling
choices.C: complicated
choices.D: hopeful

explanation.why: The early view was that the call was "a simple alarm with a single meaning." The experiments show calls that differ by predator and responses that differ too. A story with several meanings and several responses is more "complicated" than a simple one.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The experiments overturned the familiar assumption rather than confirming it.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The findings are about how varied the calls are; the text expresses no worry about them.
explanation.C: Correct. Several calls and several responses make a more complicated picture than one call meaning "danger."
explanation.D: Incorrect. Nothing in the text suggests the findings are good news or bad news; they are simply more detailed.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: Qissa Khwani Bazaar, in the old city of Peshawar, Pakistan, takes its name from the Persian for "storytellers." For centuries the bazaar was the last stop before the Khyber Pass, and caravans from Central Asia and India rested there before moving on. In the evenings, merchants gathered at the tea stalls, where professional storytellers recited tales of heroes and travelers for whoever would pay. The bazaar still ______ with trade, but the storytellers are gone; today the name is the main reminder of the audiences who once sat late into the night listening to them.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: competes
choices.B: bustles
choices.C: experiments
choices.D: struggles

explanation.why: The sentence sets up a contrast with "still" and "but": one feature of the bazaar continues while another, the storytellers, has ended. The feature that continues is the busy trade of a market, so "bustles with trade" fits.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The bazaar is not competing with trade; trade is what fills it.
explanation.B: Correct. The bazaar is still busy with trade even though the storytellers have disappeared.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Nothing in the text suggests the bazaar is trying new things.
explanation.D: Incorrect. A bazaar that "struggles" would not contrast with the loss of the storytellers; "still" signals that the trade continues as before.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: Coir, the stiff fiber that surrounds a coconut's hard shell, has been twisted into rope along the coast of Kerala, in southern India, for centuries. Preparing it is slow. Husks are soaked in shallow lagoons for months until the soft tissue around the fibers rots away, then beaten and combed by hand before the fiber can be spun. The effort was worth it to sailors because coir rope, unlike rope made from most plant fibers, does not ______ in seawater; a line that would quickly rot on a ship fitted with hemp could last for years when made of coir.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: stiffen
choices.B: soften
choices.C: deteriorate
choices.D: stretch

explanation.why: The clause after the semicolon explains the blank: a hemp line "would quickly rot" at sea, while a coir line "could last for years." So coir does not break down in seawater, which is what "deteriorate" means.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Becoming stiff is not the problem the text describes; the problem with other fibers is that they rot.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The comparison is about rotting and lasting, not about how soft the rope becomes.
explanation.C: Correct. Hemp rots quickly in seawater and coir lasts for years, so coir does not deteriorate.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Nothing in the text concerns the rope's length or stretch.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: For much of the twentieth century, tea sold at railway stations across northern India came in a kulhad, a small unglazed clay cup made by local potters. The cup was used once and then thrown onto the ground, where it broke and returned to the soil within weeks. In the 1990s, plastic and paper cups ______ the kulhad on most platforms, because they were cheaper and lighter. The change had a cost that was easy to miss: the discarded cups did not break down, and the potters who had supplied stations lost a steady market. Several campaigns have since tried to bring the clay cup back.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: displaced
choices.B: resembled
choices.C: preceded
choices.D: complemented

explanation.why: The potters "lost a steady market," and later campaigns tried "to bring the clay cup back." Both details show that plastic and paper cups took the kulhad's place, so "displaced" is the precise word.
explanation.A: Correct. The new cups pushed out the kulhad, which is why the potters lost their market and campaigns later tried to restore the clay cup.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text contrasts the cups (one breaks down, the others do not); it never says they looked alike.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This reverses the order of events: the kulhad was used first, and plastic and paper cups came later.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The new cups did not add to the kulhad; they took its place, as the lost market shows.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: When plans for the Eiffel Tower were announced in 1887, a group of prominent writers and artists published a letter calling it a useless and monstrous iron shaft that would disgrace Paris. The engineer Gustave Eiffel answered the aesthetic objection with an engineering one. The tower's sweeping curve, he explained, was not a decoration; it was the shape that the wind demanded. He had calculated the pressure a gale would exert at every height and ______ the width of the structure accordingly, so that the tower's form was, in his view, a kind of beauty produced by necessity.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: ignored
choices.B: doubled
choices.C: adjusted
choices.D: disguised

explanation.why: Eiffel calculated wind pressure "at every height" and set the width "accordingly," that is, to match those calculations. The curve is "the shape that the wind demanded." Changing the width to fit the calculation at each height is to "adjust" it.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Eiffel based the width on his calculations; he did not ignore it.
explanation.B: Incorrect. "Accordingly" means the width followed the wind calculation at each height; it was not simply doubled everywhere.
explanation.C: Correct. He set the width at each height to match the wind pressure he had calculated, which is adjusting it.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Eiffel insisted the curve was "not a decoration"; he was explaining the structure, not hiding it.

items.subject: science
items.passage: The Cingino Dam, in the Italian Alps, is a wall of stone blocks that rises almost vertically for fifty meters. Visitors are regularly startled to see Alpine ibex, wild goats with heavy curved horns, standing on its face, picking their way along ledges only a few centimeters wide. The animals are not there for the view. The mortar between the blocks contains mineral salts that the ibex need and cannot easily find in their grassy pastures, and they have learned that the dam ______ what the pasture lacks. The climb is dangerous, but the reward appears to be worth the risk.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: requires
choices.B: supplies
choices.C: conceals
choices.D: destroys

explanation.why: The ibex "need" mineral salts, cannot find them in their pastures, and climb the dam because its mortar "contains" them. The dam therefore provides what the pasture lacks, and "supplies" says exactly that.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The ibex, not the dam, need the salts; the dam is their source.
explanation.B: Correct. The mortar provides the mineral salts that the pastures lack, which is why the ibex climb.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The dam makes the salts available to the ibex; it does not hide them.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The dam gives the ibex something valuable; it does not destroy anything.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: The morin khuur, or horsehead fiddle, is the national instrument of Mongolia. It has only two strings, traditionally made of horsehair, and a carved horse's head at the top of its neck. Players draw a bow across the strings and shift the pitch not by pressing the strings to the neck, as a violinist does, but by touching them from the side with the fingertips and nails. The technique allows the player to ______ the sounds of a horse: a slow bowed note can resemble a long whinny, and quick slides can suggest the rhythm of hooves. Herders say the instrument's voice belongs to the open steppe.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: record
choices.B: evoke
choices.C: silence
choices.D: measure

explanation.why: The colon gives examples: a note "can resemble a long whinny," and slides "can suggest the rhythm of hooves." The player brings the sounds of a horse to the listener's mind, which is to "evoke" them.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The instrument does not capture real horse sounds; it produces notes that merely "resemble" and "suggest" them.
explanation.B: Correct. The playing technique calls up, or evokes, the sounds of a horse through resemblance and suggestion.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The player produces horse-like sounds rather than stopping them.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Nothing in the text involves measuring sounds.

items.subject: science
items.passage: Quinoa, a grain-like seed grown in the Andes for thousands of years, arrives at the market with a problem built in. Each seed is coated in saponins, bitter compounds that foam in water and taste soapy. The coating is not a flaw from the plant's point of view: it ______ birds and insects that would otherwise strip a field of its seeds. For cooks, though, it is a nuisance, and quinoa must be rinsed or rubbed thoroughly before it is edible. Plant breeders have developed varieties with little saponin, but these, predictably, suffer more damage from birds.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: attracts
choices.B: repels
choices.C: conceals
choices.D: poisons

explanation.why: The bitter coating is useful to the plant because of its effect on "birds and insects that would otherwise strip a field." The last sentence confirms it: varieties with little saponin "suffer more damage from birds." So the coating keeps the animals away, which is what "repels" means.
explanation.A: Incorrect. This reverses the logic: a coating that drew birds in would not protect the field.
explanation.B: Correct. The bitter, soapy taste drives birds and insects away, protecting the seeds.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The coating does not hide the seeds; the birds avoid them because of the taste.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text describes the coating as bitter and soapy, not deadly; the effect is that animals avoid the seeds, not that they die.

items.subject: humanities
items.passage: The quality of a hand-knotted Persian carpet is often judged by knot density, the number of knots tied in each square centimeter of the weave. A fine carpet may have several hundred; a coarse one, a few dozen. Density matters because it determines how much ______ a design can have: with more knots, the weaver can render a curling vine or a tiny bird in smooth outlines, where a coarser weave would show them as blocky steps. But density is bought with time. Doubling the knots in a carpet roughly doubles the months a weaver must spend at the loom.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: color
choices.B: value
choices.C: symmetry
choices.D: detail

explanation.why: The colon explains the blank: more knots let the weaver show "a curling vine or a tiny bird in smooth outlines," while fewer knots give "blocky steps." What density controls is how fine and precise the design can be, which is its "detail."
explanation.A: Incorrect. The examples are about the fineness of outlines, not about how many colors a carpet can use.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Density may affect a carpet's worth, but the sentence after the colon explains what the design can show, not what it costs.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Nothing in the text concerns whether a design is balanced or mirrored.
explanation.D: Correct. More knots allow finer outlines and smaller figures, that is, more detail in the design.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: In the nineteenth century, the slate quarries of North Wales roofed much of the industrializing world. Slate was ideal for the purpose: it splits cleanly into thin sheets, sheds water, and does not burn. Splitting it was a craft in itself. A quarryman set a chisel against the edge of a block and tapped it with a mallet, feeling for the natural plane along which the stone would part. A well-struck block yielded a sheet only a few millimeters thick; a poorly judged one ______, and the block was wasted. Machines were tried, but for decades none matched the hand's sense of where the stone wanted to break.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: shattered
choices.B: hardened
choices.C: burned
choices.D: warped

explanation.why: The sentence contrasts a well-struck block, which gives a clean thin sheet, with a poorly judged one, after which "the block was wasted." A strike in the wrong place breaks the stone into useless pieces, so "shattered" fits.
explanation.A: Correct. A badly judged blow breaks the block into pieces instead of a clean sheet, wasting it.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Nothing in the text suggests the stone changes hardness; the problem with a bad strike is breakage.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text says plainly that slate "does not burn."
explanation.D: Incorrect. Stone does not bend out of shape; the text describes it parting along a plane or breaking.

items.subject: history_social
items.passage: On the cliffs of the Azores, a chain of Portuguese islands in the mid-Atlantic, stand small whitewashed huts called vigias. For more than a century, men sat in them from dawn to dusk scanning the sea for the spout of a sperm whale, and when one was sighted they set off a rocket to summon the boats. Whaling ended in the islands in the 1980s, but the vigias were not ______. Today lookouts with binoculars still work from the same huts, radioing the position of whales to tour boats carrying visitors who have come to watch the animals rather than hunt them.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: abandoned
choices.B: needed
choices.C: repurposed
choices.D: visible

explanation.why: "But" sets up a contrast with the end of whaling, and the next sentence says lookouts "still work from the same huts." So the huts were not given up when whaling stopped: they were not "abandoned."
explanation.A: Correct. The huts stayed in use after whaling ended, so they were not abandoned.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The huts are still used every day by lookouts, so they clearly are still needed.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This reverses the point: the huts were in fact given a new purpose, serving tour boats instead of whalers.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Nothing in the text is about whether the huts can be seen.

items.subject: science
items.passage: Fire ants build their nests in soil, and in the floodplains where many of them live, heavy rain can fill a nest within hours. Individually, a fire ant that falls into water struggles to stay afloat. Collectively, however, the ants ______ flooding: when water rises through their nest, workers grip one another by their legs and jaws, forming a raft that can float for weeks, and the air trapped among their bodies keeps even the ants on the bottom layer from drowning.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

choices.A: prevent
choices.B: withstand
choices.C: ignore
choices.D: anticipate

explanation.why: "Individually" and "Collectively, however" set up a contrast: alone, an ant "struggles to stay afloat," but together the ants form a raft that "can float for weeks." The blank must mean that the group survives or holds up against the flood, which is what "withstand" means.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The ants cannot stop the water from rising; the text says they float on it. Their raft is a response to flooding, not a way of keeping it from occurring.
explanation.B: Correct. The contrast with the single ant that "struggles to stay afloat" shows that the group holds up against flooding, surviving on a raft "for weeks."
explanation.C: Incorrect. The ants respond actively to the water by gripping one another and forming a raft, which is the opposite of taking no notice of it.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text describes what the ants do once "water rises through their nest," not any ability to predict a flood before it happens.
